As an Admin, I want to be the only one who can make content public, so that officers can draft freely without risking an accidental public mistake.\n23\t13. As an Editor, I want a clear, specific message if I try to publish a Post, so that I understand I need an Admin's help rather than assuming something is broken.\n24\t14. As an Admin or Editor, I want each Post to have a title, a URL slug, a Markdown body, an author, and created/updated timestamps, so that readers and editors know what it is, when it happened, and who wrote it.\n25\t15. As an Editor, I want to create and edit static Pages (About, Eligibility, Events, Roster, Join), so that evergreen chapter information stays current.\n26\t16. As an Admin, I want published Pages to appear automatically in the public site's navigation, so that I never have to hand-edit a menu when a Page changes.\n27\t17. As a prospective member, I want an Eligibility page stating the 3.5+ GPA (across 2+ CS courses) and application requirement, so that I know whether and how to apply.\n28\t18. As a current Member, I want the 20+ CS-related service-hours requirement described as something completed *during* membership (not before joining), so that I don't mistakenly think I'm not yet eligible to apply.\n29\t19. As a prospective member, I want a Join page with clear instructions and the advisor's contact email (dkahle@uaschools.org), so that I know how to actually apply.\n30\t20. As a public visitor, I want a Roster page listing the President by name and other officers as Volunteers, so that I know who runs the chapter.\n31\t21. As an Admin, I want to create a new user account for an officer, so that they can start contributing without me editing content on their behalf.\n32\t22. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role between admin and editor, so that responsibilities can shift as chapter leadership changes.\n33\t23. As an Admin, I want to deactivate a user's account, so that a graduated or former officer immediately loses access.\n34\t24. As a deactivated user, I want to be refused login with a clear message, so that I understand my access was intentionally revoked, not broken.\n35\t25. As an Editor, I want to be refused access to user-management pages, so that officer accounts can't be tampered with by mistake or malice.\n36\t26. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing content counts by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n37\t27. As an Admin or Editor, I want to filter the content list by status (draft/published) or type (post/page), so that I can find what I'm looking for without scrolling through everything.\n38\t28. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear success or error message after every save, so that I know my change actually took effect.\n39\t29. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n40\t30. As a public visitor, I want to see only published content, never drafts, so that I'm not confused by unfinished or incorrect information.\n41\t31. As an Admin, I want a single publish command that regenerates the public site from exactly the currently-published content, so that the live site never drifts from what's actually approved.\n42\t32. As an Admin, I want the published site to use only relative links, so that it works correctly at its GitHub Pages subfolder URL.\n43\t33. As a public visitor or Admin/Editor on a phone, I want the site and admin console to work without horizontal scrolling, so that I can read announcements or manage content from my phone.\n44\t34. As an Admin, I want any Markdown a user submits to be sanitized before it's rendered anywhere (admin preview or public export), so that a malicious `<script>` tag in a post can't run in anyone's browser.\n45\t35. As an Admin, I want every content-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that a malicious link elsewhere on the web can't silently publish or delete on my behalf while I'm logged in.\n46\t36. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login if I try to reach an admin page directly, so that the admin console is never accidentally exposed.\n47\t37. As the chapter's webmaster (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n48\t\n49\t## Implementation Decisions\n50\t\n51\t- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM. `pyproject.toml`'s dependency list (fixed by the assignment) has no ORM in it, and adding one would need to be asked for separately.\n52\t- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`), since a Page is explicitly \"the same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public navigation.\" Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft` | `published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs are unique per kind, not globally, since a Post and a Page render to different URL shapes.\n53\t- **Sessions**: signed, stateless session cookies via `itsdangerous` (already a fixed dependency) — no server-side session store.\n54\t- **Passwords**: hashed with `argon2-cffi` (already a fixed dependency), satisfying the rubric's D1 check directly.\n55\t- **CSRF**: no CSRF-specific dependency exists in `pyproject.toml`, so tokens are hand-rolled — signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility used for sessions, embedded as a hidden field in every state-changing form, and verified server-side before the action runs.\n56\t- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown to HTML; the HTML output is then passed through `nh3` before it is stored or rendered anywhere. The same sanitized HTML is used in both the admin preview and the static export, so a single code path — not two — determines what a reader ever sees (rubric D4 checks both places).\n57\t- **Access control**: a shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie and exposes three guards: authenticated (any role), editor-or-admin, and admin-only. An anonymous visitor hitting an admin route is redirected to login; an authenticated user without the required role gets 403.\n58\t- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (create, edit, delete) on any Post or Page, including another user's drafts, but cannot publish/unpublish and cannot reach user-management routes. Admins can do everything Editors can, plus publish/unpublish and manage user accounts (create, change role, deactivate).\n59\t- **Publish/export**: `app/publish.py`'s `render_site()` is extended to iterate published content only — Pages render at the site root and populate the nav; Posts render under a `posts/` path and populate the home feed. Every generated `href`/`src` stays relative, respecting the existing `BASE_PATH` setting for the Pages subfolder deployment. `cms deploy` (already implemented) is unchanged.\n60\t- **Roster/Eligibility/Join/Events content**: per ADR-003, these are ordinary Pages whose Markdown body is hand-edited by an Editor or Admin — no dedicated `Officer` or `Event` data model.\n61\t\n62\t## Testing Decisions\n63\t\n64\t- Tests assert only on external, observable behavior reached through `TestClient` — HTTP status codes, redirect targets, response body content, and cookies — never on internal function calls or ORM/query internals. The one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to confirm password hashes use the `$argon2` prefix (D1), matching the rubric's own stated check method.\n65\t- All tests reuse the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`; `DEMO_USERS` there is extended to match whatever `scripts/seed_demo.py` grows into.\n66\t- Access-control tests assert exact codes per rubric D3: an editor gets 403 (or a redirect) on every admin-only route; an anonymous visitor is redirected to login on every admin route.\n67\t- CSRF tests replay one state-changing POST per form without the token and assert it's rejected (D2).\n68\t- Sanitization tests submit a Post body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publish it, and assert neither executes or appears unescaped in the admin preview response or the exported static HTML (D4).\n69\t- Publish/export tests extend the existing pattern in `tests/test_t00.py` (call `render_site()`, assert on the filesystem output) rather than introducing a new testing style: only published content appears in `site/`, drafts never do, and every `href`/`src` is relative.\n70\t\n71\t## Out of Scope\n72\t\n73\t- Dynamic Roster and Events content types (structured officer/event data) — per ADR-003, these ship as ordinary Pages in this spec.\n74\t- Revision history with rollback, and scheduled publishing — chosen as extra-credit stretch goals, tracked as separate `stretch` issues, not part of this spec's core tickets.\n75\t- Any other rubric stretch goal not explicitly chosen: media uploads, categories/tags, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, the branch+PR ticket workflow, or a secured live admin deploy.\n76\t- A functional contact/join submission form — the Join page is static content with a `mailto:` link only.\n77\t- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, a live database) — ruled out by ADR-001; the public site is a static export.\n78\t- Hosting the admin console itself on the public internet — it runs locally only, per ADR-001.\n79\t\n80\t## Further Notes\n81\t\n82\t- Client: Upper Arlington High School's CSTA-affiliated Computer Science Honor Society (CSHS) chapter. Advisor: Dr. Diane Kahle, holding the `admin` role. Full vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`.\n83\t- Stack is fixed by ADR-001 and ADR-002 (assignment-mandated), not decided in this spec: FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2-cffi, markdown-it-py, nh3, itsdangerous, ghp-import.\n84\t- This spec covers all 7 rubric-required capabilities (login, roles, posts, pages, admin console, user management, publish) in full. Any change to an announcement, the eligibility rules, the officer roster, or the join instructions requires hand-editing HTML and a developer's help. There's also no way to control who can make the site's content public, or to revoke a graduated officer's access.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small web CMS with a local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja2 + SQLite) where the Advisor and officers log in, and create, edit, delete, and — for Admins — publish Posts and Pages. A `cms publish` / `cms deploy` step renders only the published content to static HTML and pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves as the chapter's public site. The admin console itself is never exposed to the public internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n3. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear error message when I enter the wrong password, so that I know to retry rather than assume the site is broken.\n4. As an Editor, I want my password stored as a secure hash, so that a database leak doesn't expose my actual password.\n5. As an Admin, I want exactly two roles (admin, editor) with different permissions, so that officers can help without being able to break the site or see private account data.\n6. As an Editor, I want to create a new Post, so that I can announce a meeting or event to the chapter and the public.\n7. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a draft, so that I can write it over multiple sessions before it's ready.\n8. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post — including one another officer started — so that the team can collaborate without waiting on the original author.\n9. As an Editor, I want to delete a Post, so that outdated or mistaken content doesn't linger.\n10. As an Editor, I want a live Markdown preview while I write, so that I know what the published post will look like before anyone else sees it.\n11. As an Admin, I want to publish or unpublish any Post, so that I control what the public actually sees.\n12. As an Admin, I want to be the only one who can make content public, so that officers can draft freely without risking an accidental public mistake.\n13. As an Editor, I want a clear, specific message if I try to publish a Post, so that I understand I need an Admin's help rather than assuming something is broken.\n14. As an Admin or Editor, I want each Post to have a title, a URL slug, a Markdown body, an author, and created/updated timestamps, so that readers and editors know what it is, when it happened, and who wrote it.\n15. As an Editor, I want to create and edit static Pages (About, Eligibility, Events, Roster, Join), so that evergreen chapter information stays current.\n16. As an Admin, I want published Pages to appear automatically in the public site's navigation, so that I never have to hand-edit a menu when a Page changes.\n17. As a prospective member, I want an Eligibility page stating the 3.5+ GPA (across 2+ CS courses) and application requirement, so that I know whether and how to apply.\n18. As a current Member, I want the 20+ CS-related service-hours requirement described as something completed *during* membership (not before joining), so that I don't mistakenly think I'm not yet eligible to apply.\n19. As a prospective member, I want a Join page with clear instructions and the advisor's contact email (dkahle@uaschools.org), so that I know how to actually apply.\n20. As a public visitor, I want a Roster page listing the President by name and other officers as Volunteers, so that I know who runs the chapter.\n21. As an Admin, I want to create a new user account for an officer, so that they can start contributing without me editing content on their behalf.\n22. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role between admin and editor, so that responsibilities can shift as chapter leadership changes.\n23. As an Admin, I want to deactivate a user's account, so that a graduated or former officer immediately loses access.\n24. As a deactivated user, I want to be refused login with a clear message, so that I understand my access was intentionally revoked, not broken.\n25. As an Editor, I want to be refused access to user-management pages, so that officer accounts can't be tampered with by mistake or malice.\n26. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing content counts by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n27. As an Admin or Editor, I want to filter the content list by status (draft/published) or type (post/page), so that I can find what I'm looking for without scrolling through everything.\n28. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear success or error message after every save, so that I know my change actually took effect.\n29. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n30. As a public visitor, I want to see only published content, never drafts, so that I'm not confused by unfinished or incorrect information.\n31. As an Admin, I want a single publish command that regenerates the public site from exactly the currently-published content, so that the live site never drifts from what's actually approved.\n32. As an Admin, I want the published site to use only relative links, so that it works correctly at its GitHub Pages subfolder URL.\n33. As a public visitor or Admin/Editor on a phone, I want the site and admin console to work without horizontal scrolling, so that I can read announcements or manage content from my phone.\n34. As an Admin, I want any Markdown a user submits to be sanitized before it's rendered anywhere (admin preview or public export), so that a malicious `<script>` tag in a post can't run in anyone's browser.\n35. As an Admin, I want every content-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that a malicious link elsewhere on the web can't silently publish or delete on my behalf while I'm logged in.\n36. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login if I try to reach an admin page directly, so that the admin console is never accidentally exposed.\n37. As the chapter's webmaster (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM. `pyproject.toml`'s dependency list (fixed by the assignment) has no ORM in it, and adding one would need to be asked for separately.\n- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`), since a Page is explicitly \"the same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public navigation.\" Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft` | `published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs are unique per kind, not globally, since a Post and a Page render to different URL shapes.\n- **Sessions**: signed, stateless session cookies via `itsdangerous` (already a fixed dependency) — no server-side session store.\n- **Passwords**: hashed with `argon2-cffi` (already a fixed dependency), satisfying the rubric's D1 check directly.\n- **CSRF**: no CSRF-specific dependency exists in `pyproject.toml`, so tokens are hand-rolled — signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility used for sessions, embedded as a hidden field in every state-changing form, and verified server-side before the action runs.\n- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown to HTML; the HTML output is then passed through `nh3` before it is stored or rendered anywhere. The same sanitized HTML is used in both the admin preview and the static export, so a single code path — not two — determines what a reader ever sees (rubric D4 checks both places).\n- **Access control**: a shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie and exposes three guards: authenticated (any role), editor-or-admin, and admin-only. An anonymous visitor hitting an admin route is redirected to login; an authenticated user without the required role gets 403.\n- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (create, edit, delete) on any Post or Page, including another user's drafts, but cannot publish/unpublish and cannot reach user-management routes. Admins can do everything Editors can, plus publish/unpublish and manage user accounts (create, change role, deactivate).\n- **Publish/export**: `app/publish.py`'s `render_site()` is extended to iterate published content only — Pages render at the site root and populate the nav; Posts render under a `posts/` path and populate the home feed. Every generated `href`/`src` stays relative, respecting the existing `BASE_PATH` setting for the Pages subfolder deployment. `cms deploy` (already implemented) is unchanged.\n- **Roster/Eligibility/Join/Events content**: per ADR-003, these are ordinary Pages whose Markdown body is hand-edited by an Editor or Admin — no dedicated `Officer` or `Event` data model.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Tests assert only on external, observable behavior reached through `TestClient` — HTTP status codes, redirect targets, response body content, and cookies — never on internal function calls or ORM/query internals. The one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to confirm password hashes use the `$argon2` prefix (D1), matching the rubric's own stated check method.\n- All tests reuse the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`; `DEMO_USERS` there is extended to match whatever `scripts/seed_demo.py` grows into.\n- Access-control tests assert exact codes per rubric D3: an editor gets 403 (or a redirect) on every admin-only route; an anonymous visitor is redirected to login on every admin route.\n- CSRF tests replay one state-changing POST per form without the token and assert it's rejected (D2).\n- Sanitization tests submit a Post body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publish it, and assert neither executes or appears unescaped in the admin preview response or the exported static HTML (D4).\n- Publish/export tests extend the existing pattern in `tests/test_t00.py` (call `render_site()`, assert on the filesystem output) rather than introducing a new testing style: only published content appears in `site/`, drafts never do, and every `href`/`src` is relative.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Dynamic Roster and Events content types (structured officer/event data) — per ADR-003, these ship as ordinary Pages in this spec.\n- Revision history with rollback, and scheduled publishing — chosen as extra-credit stretch goals, tracked as separate `stretch` issues, not part of this spec's core tickets.\n- Any other rubric stretch goal not explicitly chosen: media uploads, categories/tags, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, the branch+PR ticket workflow, or a secured live admin deploy.\n- A functional contact/join submission form — the Join page is static content with a `mailto:` link only.\n- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, a live database) — ruled out by ADR-001; As a deactivated user, I want to be refused login with a clear message, so that I understand my access was intentionally revoked, not broken.\n25. As an Editor, I want to be refused access to user-management pages, so that officer accounts can't be tampered with by mistake or malice.\n26. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing content counts by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n27. As an Admin or Editor, I want to filter the content list by status (draft/published) or type (post/page), so that I can find what I'm looking for without scrolling through everything.\n28. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear success or error message after every save, so that I know my change actually took effect.\n29. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n30. As a public visitor, I want to see only published content, never drafts, so that I'm not confused by unfinished or incorrect information.\n31. As an Admin, I want a single publish command that regenerates the public site from exactly the currently-published content, so that the live site never drifts from what's actually approved.\n32. As an Admin, I want the published site to use only relative links, so that it works correctly at its GitHub Pages subfolder URL.\n33. As a public visitor or Admin/Editor on a phone, I want the site and admin console to work without horizontal scrolling, so that I can read announcements or manage content from my phone.\n34. As an Admin, I want any Markdown a user submits to be sanitized before it's rendered anywhere (admin preview or public export), so that a malicious `<script>` tag in a post can't run in anyone's browser.\n35. As an Admin, I want every content-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that a malicious link elsewhere on the web can't silently publish or delete on my behalf while I'm logged in.\n36. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login if I try to reach an admin page directly, so that the admin console is never accidentally exposed.\n37. As the chapter's webmaster (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM — none is in the fixed `pyproject.toml` dependency list.\n- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`). Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs unique per kind.\n- **Sessions**: signed, stateless cookies via `itsdangerous` — no server-side session store.\n- **Passwords**: `argon2-cffi` hashing (satisfies rubric D1 directly).\n- **CSRF**: hand-rolled token signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility as sessions, embedded in every state-changing form, verified server-side. No dedicated CSRF library exists in the fixed dependencies.\n- **Markdown/sanitization**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown → HTML, then `nh3` sanitizes that HTML. One code path feeds both the admin preview and the static export (rubric D4 checks both).\n- **Access control**: one shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie; three guards — authenticated, editor-or-admin, admin-only. Anonymous → redirect to login; wrong role → 403.\n- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (including delete) on any content, including others' drafts, but no publish/unpublish and no user management. Admins get everything Editors get, plus those two.\n- **Publish/export**: `render_site()` extended to emit only published content — Pages at site root (and into the nav), Posts under `posts/` (and into the home feed) — relative paths throughout, respecting `BASE_PATH`. `cms deploy` unchanged.\n- **Roster/Eligibility/Join/Events**: ordinary Pages (ADR-003) — no dedicated data model.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Assert only on external behavior via `TestClient` (status codes, redirects, response body, cookies) — one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to check the `$argon2` hash prefix (D1), per the rubric's own check method.\n- Reuse `client` / `client_as(role)` from `tests/conftest.py`; extend `DEMO_USERS` alongside `scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n- Access-control tests: editor → 403/redirect on every admin-only route; anonymous → redirect to login (D3).\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per form without the token, assert rejection (D2).\n- Sanitization tests: submit `<script>` + `onerror=`, publish, assert neither survives in the preview or the export (D4).\n- Publish/export tests extend the existing `tests/test_t00.py` pattern (call `render_site()`, assert on filesystem output): published-only, drafts never leak, relative paths only.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Dynamic Roster/Events data models (ADR-003 — ship as Pages).\n- Revision history with rollback, scheduled publishing — separate `stretch` issues.\n- All other rubric stretch goals not chosen (media uploads, categories/tags, search, comments, plugins, themes, branch+PR workflow, secured live admin deploy).\n- A functional contact/join form — static Page + `mailto:` only.\n- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, live DB) — ADR-001.\n- Hosting the admin console publicly — ADR-001, local-only.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Client: Upper Arlington HS's CSTA-affiliated CSHS chapter. Advisor: Dr. Diane Kahle (`admin`). Full vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`.\n- Stack fixed by ADR-001/ADR-002, not decided here.\n- Covers all 7 rubric-required capabilities in full; extra credit gets its own issues later.\n\n---\n\nLet me know if anything needs changing. Once you approve and have run `gh auth login`, I'll create the GitHub repo and post this as the `spec`-labeled issue."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4462,"cache_read_input_tokens":153673,"output_tokens":3888,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":398},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4462,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3888,"cache_read_input_tokens":153673,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4462,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4462},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"7789bb74-9947-421c-b1f1-e53614493072","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfYGM85Sgn2Jb3iv4KShy","type":"assistant","uuid":"d650a4bd-0bd4-4905-8071-3ce8c2530a46","timestamp":"2026-09-29T19:15:30.539Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.282","gitBranch":"master"}

{"parentUuid":"1a2200a9-e6db-4977-ac28-23b6bba0911a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011Cfby4Fv3GmNHT5zBrjNS6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011AvhHtTdgA88r5dd3efR4m","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > \"C:/Rajan/E disk/My work/IPHS400/code/mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md\" << 'EOF'\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS: a local admin console where Editors and Admins manage content, and a static public site that publishes it. The content model is intentionally generic — built with no specific client in mind. (A specific client site will be built *using* this CMS as a later, separate project.)\n\n## Roles\n\n**Admin**:\nA CMS user role with full permissions: everything an Editor can do, plus publishing/unpublishing content and managing user accounts (create, change role, deactivate).\n_Avoid_: superadmin, owner\n\n**Editor**:\nA CMS user role that can create, edit, and delete any Post or Page — including another user's drafts — but cannot publish/unpublish content or manage user accounts.\n_Avoid_: contributor, author (an Author is a content attribute, not a role)\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**:\nA dated, feed-like content item with a title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, and timestamps. Appears in the site's chronological feed.\n_Avoid_: article, entry\n\n**Page**:\nA static, evergreen content item — same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public site's navigation once published.\n_Avoid_: static page (redundant)\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe identifier for a Post or Page, unique within its kind, used to build its published path.\n\n**Status (Draft / Published)**:\nThe two states a Post or Page can be in. A Draft is visible only in the admin console; only a Published item reaches the static export.\n_Avoid_: live/unlive, active/inactive\n\n**Author**:\nThe user (Admin or Editor) recorded as having written a given Post or Page. Distinct from whoever most recently edited it.\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Publish** (verb):\nThe admin-only action that flips a content item's status from Draft to Published, making it eligible to appear in the next static export.\n_Avoid_: approve (there's no separate approval workflow — publish is a single, direct action)\n\n**Static export**:\nThe `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages.\n\n**Revision history** _(stretch goal)_:\nA record of a Post or Page's prior saved versions, with the ability to roll back to one.\n\n**Scheduled publishing** _(stretch goal)_:\nSetting a future date/time at which a Draft automatically becomes Published, with no manual step at that time.\nEOF\necho \"written\"","description":"Write generic CONTEXT.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":543,"cache_read_input_tokens":214085,"output_tokens":1238,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":265},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":543,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1238,"cache_read_input_tokens":214085,"cache_creation_input_tokens":543,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":543},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_011AvhHtTdgA88r5dd3efR4m":{"command":"cat > \"C:/Rajan/E disk/My work/IPHS400/code/mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md\" << 'EOF'\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS: a local admin console where Editors and Admins manage content, and a static public site that publishes it. {"parentUuid":"275f3859-5505-4674-b96f-3bb829fd3660","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"33c52c84-83d2-4db5-bf01-a6c14026e6d5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019T3d98AfeUhV7tLCkoZNMn","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-003: Roster and Events are Pages, not dedicated content types\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** accepted\n4\t**Date:** 2026-09-29\n5\t\n6\t## Context\n7\t\n8\tA WordPress-style CMS would typically model a member roster and an events\n9\tcalendar as their own structured content types (a roster entry with a photo\n10\tand role field; an event with a date, time, and location field). The rubric's\n11\textra-credit list is fixed and closed — exactly ten named stretch goals,\n12\tcapped at 5 points total — and neither a roster type nor an events type is on\n13\tit. Building either as real structured data would cost implementation time\n14\twithout moving the grade, and Stage 1's deadline is tight.\n15\t\n16\t## Decision\n17\t\n18\tRoster and Events ship as ordinary Pages (About, Eligibility, Events, Roster,\n19\tJoin) using the same Post/Page Markdown editor as everything else. No\n20\t`Officer` or `Event` database model exists. The Roster page's officer names,\n21\tand the Events page's meeting schedule, are edited as plain Markdown text\n22\tlike any other Page content.\n23\t\n24\t## Consequences\n25\t\n26\t- Officers are added, removed, or reordered by hand-editing the Roster Page's\n27\t  body — there's no per-officer form, photo field, or validation.\n28\t- Event dates are prose in a Page, not queryable data — no calendar view,\n29\t  sorting, or \"next meeting\" widget is possible without a later model change.\n30\t- If the live chapter site later wants structured roster/events data, that's\n31\t  a new content type built on top of the existing Post/Page pattern, not a\n32\t  migration away from one.\n33\t\n34\t## Why this is an ADR\n35\t\n36\tIt's a deliberate deviation from the obvious path — a CMS reader would expect\n37\ta roster and an events calendar to be modeled as data — and it's driven by a\n38\tconstraint (the closed extra-credit list plus the deadline) that isn't\n39\tvisible anywhere else in the code.\n40\t</content>\n41\t"}]},"uuid":"b8e13c95-9e2c-4e9b-85ee-2bdbe11e7fd6","timestamp":"2026-10-01T18:10:56.352Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\docs\\adr\\ADR-003-roster-events-as-pages.md","content":"# ADR-003: Roster and Events are Pages, not dedicated content types\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-09-29\n\n## Context\n\nA WordPress-style CMS would typically model a member roster and an events\ncalendar as their own structured content types (a roster entry with a photo\nand role field; an event with a date, time, and location field). The rubric's\nextra-credit list is fixed and closed — exactly ten named stretch goals,\ncapped at 5 points total — and neither a roster type nor an events type is on\nit. Building either as real structured data would cost implementation time\nwithout moving the grade, and Stage 1's deadline is tight.\n\n## Decision\n\nRoster and Events ship as ordinary Pages (About, Eligibility, Events, Roster,\nJoin) using the same Post/Page Markdown editor as everything else. No\n`Officer` or `Event` database model exists. The Roster page's officer names,\nand the Events page's meeting schedule, are edited as plain Markdown text\nlike any other Page content.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Officers are added, removed, or reordered by hand-editing the Roster Page's\n  body — there's no per-officer form, photo field, or validation.\n- Event dates are prose in a Page, not queryable data — no calendar view,\n  sorting, or \"next meeting\" widget is possible without a later model change.\n- If the live chapter site later wants structured roster/events data, that's\n  a new content type built on top of the existing Post/Page pattern, not a\n  migration away from one.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt's a deliberate deviation from the obvious path — a CMS reader would expect\na roster and an events calendar to be modeled as data — and it's driven by a\nconstraint (the closed extra-credit list plus the deadline) that isn't\nvisible anywhere else in the code.\n</content>\n","numLines":41,"startLine":1,"totalLines":41}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"275f3859-5505-4674-b96f-3bb829fd3660","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"4183f8e4-b693-4193-b1d0-cc764a6e2250","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011Cfby5VoVzxV6MUNpAGShD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01BHmtmCEMtkUs3D3HcHtsUT","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\spec-draft.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nSomeone running a small website has no self-service way to keep it up to date: publishing an announcement, editing a static page, or controlling who can make content public all require hand-editing HTML or a developer's help. There's also no way to grant a collaborator limited access, or revoke it later, without touching the server directly.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS with a local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja2 + SQLite) where Admins and Editors log in and create, edit, delete, and — for Admins — publish Posts and Pages. A `cms publish` / `cms deploy` step renders only the published content to static HTML and pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves as the public site. The admin console itself is never exposed to the public internet. The content model is intentionally generic — this build is not shaped around any specific client; a specific site will be built on top of this CMS afterward, as a separate project.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n3. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear error message when I enter the wrong password, so that I know to retry rather than assume the site is broken.\n4. As an Editor, I want my password stored as a secure hash, so that a database leak doesn't expose my actual password.\n5. As an Admin, I want exactly two roles (admin, editor) with different permissions, so that a collaborator can help without being able to break the site or see private account data.\n6. As an Editor, I want to create a new Post, so that I can publish a dated piece of content to the site's feed.\n7. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a draft, so that I can write it over multiple sessions before it's ready.\n8. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post — including one another Editor started — so that a team can collaborate without waiting on the original author.\n9. As an Editor, I want to delete a Post, so that outdated or mistaken content doesn't linger.\n10. As an Editor, I want a live Markdown preview while I write, so that I know what the published post will look like before anyone else sees it.\n11. As an Admin, I want to publish or unpublish any Post, so that I control what the public actually sees.\n12. As an Admin, I want to be the only one who can make content public, so that Editors can draft freely without risking an accidental public mistake.\n13. As an Editor, I want a clear, specific message if I try to publish a Post, so that I understand I need an Admin's help rather than assuming something is broken.\n14. As an Admin or Editor, I want each Post to have a title, a URL slug, a Markdown body, an author, and created/updated timestamps, so that readers and editors know what it is, when it happened, and who wrote it.\n15. As an Editor, I want to create and edit static Pages, so that evergreen site information (e.g. an About page) stays current.\n16. As an Admin, I want published Pages to appear automatically in the public site's navigation, so that I never have to hand-edit a menu when a Page changes.\n17. As an Admin, I want to create a new user account for a collaborator, so that they can start contributing without me editing content on their behalf.\n18. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role between admin and editor, so that responsibilities can shift as a team changes.\n19. As an Admin, I want to deactivate a user's account, so that someone who leaves the team immediately loses access.\n20. As a deactivated user, I want to be refused login with a clear message, so that I understand my access was intentionally revoked, not broken.\n21. As an Editor, I want to be refused access to user-management pages, so that accounts can't be tampered with by mistake or malice.\n22. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing content counts by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n23. As an Admin or Editor, I want to filter the content list by status (draft/published) or type (post/page), so that I can find what I'm looking for without scrolling through everything.\n24. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear success or error message after every save, so that I know my change actually took effect.\n25. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n26. As a public visitor, I want to see only published content, never drafts, so that I'm not confused by unfinished or incorrect information.\n27. As an Admin, I want a single publish command that regenerates the public site from exactly the currently-published content, so that the live site never drifts from what's actually approved.\n28. As an Admin, I want the published site to use only relative links, so that it works correctly at its GitHub Pages subfolder URL.\n29. As a public visitor or Admin/Editor on a phone, I want the site and admin console to work without horizontal scrolling, so that I can read content or manage it from my phone.\n30. As an Admin, I want any Markdown a user submits to be sanitized before it's rendered anywhere (admin preview or public export), so that a malicious `<script>` tag in a post can't run in anyone's browser.\n31. As an Admin, I want every content-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that a malicious link elsewhere on the web can't silently publish or delete on my behalf while I'm logged in.\n32. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login if I try to reach an admin page directly, so that the admin console is never accidentally exposed.\n33. As the site's operator (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM — none is in the fixed `pyproject.toml` dependency list.\n- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`). Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs unique per kind.\n- **Sessions**: signed, stateless cookies via `itsdangerous` — no server-side session store.\n- **Passwords**: `argon2-cffi` hashing (satisfies rubric D1 directly).\n- **CSRF**: hand-rolled token signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility as sessions, embedded in every state-changing form, verified server-side. No dedicated CSRF library exists in the fixed dependencies.\n- **Markdown/sanitization**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown → HTML, then `nh3` sanitizes that HTML. One code path feeds both the admin preview and the static export (rubric D4 checks both).\n- **Access control**: one shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie; three guards — authenticated, editor-or-admin, admin-only. Anonymous → redirect to login; wrong role → 403.\n- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (including delete) on any content, including others' drafts, but no publish/unpublish and no user management. Admins get everything Editors get, plus those two.\n- **Publish/export**: `render_site()` extended to emit only published content — Pages at site root (and into the nav), Posts under `posts/` (and into the home feed) — relative paths throughout, respecting `BASE_PATH`. `cms deploy` unchanged.\n- **Demo/seed content**: neutral placeholders only (e.g. a generic site title, example posts/pages) — no client brief, real or fictional, baked into seed data or the schema.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Assert only on external behavior via `TestClient` (status codes, redirects, response body, cookies) — one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to check the `$argon2` hash prefix (D1), per the rubric's own check method.\n- Reuse `client` / `client_as(role)` from `tests/conftest.py`; extend `DEMO_USERS` alongside `scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n- Access-control tests: editor → 403/redirect on every admin-only route; anonymous → redirect to login (D3).\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per form without the token, assert rejection (D2).\n- Sanitization tests: submit `<script>` + `onerror=`, publish, assert neither survives in the preview or the export (D4).\n- Publish/export tests extend the existing `tests/test_t00.py` pattern (call `render_site()`, assert on filesystem output): published-only, drafts never leak, relative paths only.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Any client-specific content, vocabulary, or data model — this build is a generic CMS engine; a specific site is a separate, later project built on top of it.\n- Revision history with rollback, scheduled publishing — separate `stretch` issues.\n- All other rubric stretch goals not chosen (media uploads, categories/tags, search, comments, plugins, themes, branch+PR workflow, secured live admin deploy).\n- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, live DB) — ADR-001.\n- Hosting the admin console publicly — ADR-001, local-only.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- This project builds the CMS engine only, with no client in mind, per the instructor's verbal direction (2026-10-01) superseding the earlier client-specific plan recorded in ADR-003 (now marked superseded, kept for the record).\n- Stack fixed by ADR-001/ADR-002, not decided here.\n- Covers all 7 rubric-required capabilities in full; extra credit gets its own issues later.\n</content>\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":471,"cache_read_input_tokens":216787,"output_tokens":3383,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":471,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3383,"cache_read_input_tokens":216787,"cache_creation_input_tokens":471,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":471},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01BHmtmCEMtkUs3D3HcHtsUT":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\spec-draft.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nSomeone running a small website has no self-service way to keep it up to date: publishing an announcement, editing a static page, or controlling who can make content public all require hand-editing HTML or a developer's help. There's also no way to grant a collaborator limited access, or revoke it later, without touching the server directly.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS with a local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja2 + SQLite) where Admins and Editors log in and create, edit, delete, and — for Admins — publish Posts and Pages. A `cms publish` / `cms deploy` step renders only the published content to static HTML and pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves as the public site. The admin console itself is never exposed to the public internet. The content model is intentionally generic — this build is not shaped around any specific client; a specific site will be built on top of this CMS afterward, as a separate project.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n3. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear error message when I enter the wrong password, so that I know to retry rather than assume the site is broken.\n4. As an Editor, I want my password stored as a secure hash, so that a database leak doesn't expose my actual password.\n5. As an Admin, I want exactly two roles (admin, editor) with different permissions, so that a collaborator can help without being able to break the site or see private account data.\n6. As the site's operator (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time."," "," ## Implementation Decisions"," ","-- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM. `pyproject.toml`'s dependency list (fixed by the assignment) has no ORM in it, and adding one would need to be asked for separately.","-- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`), since a Page is explicitly \"the same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public navigation.\" Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft` | `published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs are unique per kind, not globally, since a Post and a Page render to different URL shapes.","-- **Sessions**: signed, stateless session cookies via `itsdangerous` (already a fixed dependency) — no server-side session store.","-- **Passwords**: hashed with `argon2-cffi` (already a fixed dependency), satisfying the rubric's D1 check directly.","-- **CSRF**: no CSRF-specific dependency exists in `pyproject.toml`, so tokens are hand-rolled — signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility used for sessions, embedded as a hidden field in every state-changing form, and verified server-side before the action runs.","-- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown to HTML; the HTML output is then passed through `nh3` before it is stored or rendered anywhere. The same sanitized HTML is used in both the admin preview and the static export, so a single code path — not two — determines what a reader ever sees (rubric D4 checks both places).","-- **Access control**: a shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie and exposes three guards: authenticated (any role), editor-or-admin, and admin-only. An anonymous visitor hitting an admin route is redirected to login; an authenticated user without the required role gets 403.","-- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (create, edit, delete) on any Post or Page, including another user's drafts, but cannot publish/unpublish and cannot reach user-management routes. Admins can do everything Editors can, plus publish/unpublish and manage user accounts (create, change role, deactivate).","-- **Publish/export**: `app/publish.py`'s `render_site()` is extended to iterate published content only — Pages render at the site root and populate the nav; Posts render under a `posts/` path and populate the home feed. Every generated `href`/`src` stays relative, respecting the existing `BASE_PATH` setting for the Pages subfolder deployment. `cms deploy` (already implemented) is unchanged.","-- **Roster/Eligibility/Join/Events content**: per ADR-003, these are ordinary Pages whose Markdown body is hand-edited by an Editor or Admin — no dedicated `Officer` or `Event` data model.","+- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM — none is in the fixed `pyproject.toml` dependency list.","+- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`). Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs unique per kind.","+- **Sessions**: signed, stateless cookies via `itsdangerous` — no server-side session store.","+- **Passwords**: `argon2-cffi` hashing (satisfies rubric D1 directly).","+- **CSRF**: hand-rolled token signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility as sessions, embedded in every state-changing form, verified server-side. No dedicated CSRF library exists in the fixed dependencies.","+- **Markdown/sanitization**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown → HTML, then `nh3` sanitizes that HTML. One code path feeds both the admin preview and the static export (rubric D4 checks both).","+- **Access control**: one shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie; three guards — authenticated, editor-or-admin, admin-only. Anonymous → redirect to login; wrong role → 403.","+- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (including delete) on any content, including others' drafts, but no publish/unpublish and no user management. Admins get everything Editors get, plus those two.","+- **Publish/export**: `render_site()` extended to emit only published content — Pages at site root (and into the nav), Posts under `posts/` (and into the home feed) — relative paths throughout, respecting `BASE_PATH`. `cms deploy` unchanged.","+- **Demo/seed content**: neutral placeholders only (e.g. a generic site title, example posts/pages) — no client brief, real or fictional, baked into seed data or the schema."," "," ## Testing Decisions"," ","-- Tests assert only on external, observable behavior reached through `TestClient` — HTTP status codes, redirect targets, response body content, and cookies — never on internal function calls or ORM/query internals. The one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to confirm password hashes use the `$argon2` prefix (D1), matching the rubric's own stated check method.","-- All tests reuse the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`; `DEMO_USERS` there is extended to match whatever `scripts/seed_demo.py` grows into.","-- Access-control tests assert exact codes per rubric D3: an editor gets 403 (or a redirect) on every admin-only route; an anonymous visitor is redirected to login on every admin route.","-- CSRF tests replay one state-changing POST per form without the token and assert it's rejected (D2).","-- Sanitization tests submit a Post body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publish it, and assert neither executes or appears unescaped in the admin preview response or the exported static HTML (D4).","-- Publish/export tests extend the existing pattern in `tests/test_t00.py` (call `render_site()`, assert on the filesystem output) rather than introducing a new testing style: only published content appears in `site/`, drafts never do, and every `href`/`src` is relative.","+- Assert only on external behavior via `TestClient` (status codes, redirects, response body, cookies) — one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to check the `$argon2` hash prefix (D1), per the rubric's own check method.","+- Reuse `client` / `client_as(role)` from `tests/conftest.py`; extend `DEMO_USERS` alongside `scripts/seed_demo.py`.","+- Access-control tests: editor → 403/redirect on every admin-only route; anonymous → redirect to login (D3).","+- CSRF tests: replay one POST per form without the token, assert rejection (D2).","+- Sanitization tests: submit `<script>` + `onerror=`, publish, assert neither survives in the preview or the export (D4).","+- Publish/export tests extend the existing `tests/test_t00.py` pattern (call `render_site()`, assert on filesystem output): published-only, drafts never leak, relative paths only."," "," ## Out of Scope"," ","-- Dynamic Roster and Events content types (structured officer/event data) — per ADR-003, these ship as ordinary Pages in this spec.","-- Revision history with rollback, and scheduled publishing — chosen as extra-credit stretch goals, tracked as separate `stretch` issues, not part of this spec's core tickets.","-- Any other rubric stretch goal not explicitly chosen: media uploads, categories/tags, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, the branch+PR ticket workflow, or a secured live admin deploy.","-- A functional contact/join submission form — the Join page is static content with a `mailto:` link only.","-- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, a live database) — ruled out by ADR-001; the public site is a static export.","-- Hosting the admin console itself on the public internet — it runs locally only, per ADR-001.","+- Any client-specific content, vocabulary, or data model — this build is a generic CMS engine; a specific site is a separate, later project built on top of it.","+- Revision history with rollback, scheduled publishing — separate `stretch` issues.","+- All other rubric stretch goals not chosen (media uploads, categories/tags, search, comments, plugins, themes, branch+PR workflow, secured live admin deploy).","+- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, live DB) — ADR-001.","+- Hosting the admin console publicly — ADR-001, local-only."," "," ## Further Notes"," ","-- Client: Upper Arlington High School's CSTA-affiliated Computer Science Honor Society (CSHS) chapter. Advisor: Dr. Diane Kahle, holding the `admin` role. Full vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`.","-- Stack is fixed by ADR-001 and ADR-002 (assignment-mandated), not decided in this spec: FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2-cffi, markdown-it-py, nh3, itsdangerous, ghp-import.","-- This spec covers all 7 rubric-required capabilities (login, roles, posts, pages, admin console, user management, publish) in full. It intentionally does not cover extra-credit stretch goals, which get their own `stretch` issues later.","+- This project builds the CMS engine only, with no client in mind, per the instructor's verbal direction (2026-10-01) superseding the earlier client-specific plan recorded in ADR-003 (now marked superseded, kept for the record).","+- Stack fixed by ADR-001/ADR-002, not decided here.","+- Covers all 7 rubric-required capabilities in full; extra credit gets its own issues later."," </content>"]}],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e45ccb36-e332-48e5-aa63-371c7c06e3b4","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"a0fd993d-2fe9-40ec-a944-5ac4d8badf9f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011Cfby7VAbfcgy3xr4dNbZu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"All reworked. Here's what changed and the new spec for your approval:\n\n**`CONTEXT.md`** — now pure generic CMS vocabulary: Admin, Editor, Post, Page, Slug, Status, Author, Publish, Static export, plus the two stretch-goal terms. No CSHS/Chapter/Advisor/Roster terms.\n\n**`ADR-003`** — marked `superseded` (not deleted) with a note explaining the pivot, so the decision trail stays honest rather than erasing that it happened.\n\n**`.env.example`** — `CMS_SITE_TITLE` changed from \"Knox County Historical Society\" to the neutral \"My CMS\".\n\n**Spec** — fully regenericized:\n\n---\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nSomeone running a small website has no self-service way to keep it up to date: publishing an announcement, editing a static page, or controlling who can make content public all require hand-editing HTML or a developer's help. There's also no way to grant a collaborator limited access, or revoke it later, without touching the server directly.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS with a local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja2 + SQLite) where Admins and Editors log in and create, edit, delete, and — for Admins — publish Posts and Pages. A `cms publish` / `cms deploy` step renders only the published content to static HTML and pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves as the public site. The admin console itself is never exposed to the public internet. The content model is intentionally generic — this build is not shaped around any specific client; a specific site will be built on top of this CMS afterward, as a separate project.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n3. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear error message when I enter the wrong password, so that I know to retry rather than assume the site is broken.\n4. As an Editor, I want my password stored as a secure hash, so that a database leak doesn't expose my actual password.\n5. As an Admin, I want exactly two roles (admin, editor) with different permissions, so that a collaborator can help without being able to break the site or see private account data.\n6. As an Editor, I want to create a new Post, so that I can publish a dated piece of content to the site's feed.\n7. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a draft, so that I can write it over multiple sessions before it's ready.\n8. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post — including one another Editor started — so that a team can collaborate without waiting on the original author.\n9. As an Editor, I want to delete a Post, so that outdated or mistaken content doesn't linger.\n10. As an Editor, I want a live Markdown preview while I write, so that I know what the published post will look like before anyone else sees it.\n11. As an Admin, I want to publish or unpublish any Post, so that I control what the public actually sees.\n12. As an Admin, I want to be the only one who can make content public, so that Editors can draft freely without risking an accidental public mistake.\n13. As an Editor, I want a clear, specific message if I try to publish a Post, so that I understand I need an Admin's help rather than assuming something is broken.\n14. As an Admin or Editor, I want each Post to have a title, a URL slug, a Markdown body, an author, and created/updated timestamps, so that readers and editors know what it is, when it happened, and who wrote it.\n15. As an Editor, I want to create and edit static Pages, so that evergreen site information (e.g. an About page) stays current.\n16. As an Admin, I want published Pages to appear automatically in the public site's navigation, so that I never have to hand-edit a menu when a Page changes.\n17. As an Admin, I want to create a new user account for a collaborator, so that they can start contributing without me editing content on their behalf.\n18. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role between admin and editor, so that responsibilities can shift as a team changes.\n19. As an Admin, I want to deactivate a user's account, so that someone who leaves the team immediately loses access.\n20. As a deactivated user, I want to be refused login with a clear message, so that I understand my access was intentionally revoked, not broken.\n21. As an Editor, I want to be refused access to user-management pages, so that accounts can't be tampered with by mistake or malice.\n22. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing content counts by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n23. As an Admin or Editor, I want to filter the content list by status (draft/published) or type (post/page), so that I can find what I'm looking for without scrolling through everything.\n24. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear success or error message after every save, so that I know my change actually took effect.\n25. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n26. As a public visitor, I want to see only published content, never drafts, so that I'm not confused by unfinished or incorrect information.\n27. As an Admin, I want a single publish command that regenerates the public site from exactly the currently-published content, so that the live site never drifts from what's actually approved.\n28. As an Admin, I want the published site to use only relative links, so that it works correctly at its GitHub Pages subfolder URL.\n29. As a public visitor or Admin/Editor on a phone, I want the site and admin console to work without horizontal scrolling, so that I can read content or manage it from my phone.\n30. As an Admin, I want any Markdown a user submits to be sanitized before it's rendered anywhere (admin preview or public export), so that a malicious `<script>` tag in a post can't run in anyone's browser.\n31. As an Admin, I want every content-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that a malicious link elsewhere on the web can't silently publish or delete on my behalf while I'm logged in.\n32. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login if I try to reach an admin page directly, so that the admin console is never accidentally exposed.\n33. As the site's operator (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n(unchanged from before — stack/model/security decisions never depended on a client) plus: **Demo/seed content** is neutral placeholders only — no client brief, real or fictional.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nNow leads with: any client-specific content, vocabulary, or data model — this build is a generic CMS engine; a specific site is a separate, later project built on top of it.\n\n---\n\nWant any changes, or should I commit these reworked files and post this as the `spec` issue?"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3548,"cache_read_input_tokens":217258,"output_tokens":2244,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3548,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2244,"cache_read_input_tokens":217258,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3548,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3548},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"e549fc00-d9ae-4ed2-8c2c-2a931185401b","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cfby7Uk3eUik7WceTUQym","type":"assistant","uuid":"3c9aabf0-b38f-4d11-b83c-5b78b4b28a0d","timestamp":"2026-10-01T18:11:41.758Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"114673dd-a994-42b0-9ad4-d5b3ec3eac31","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e3d5aadd-6f46-46cc-bbf9-1346b1e28714","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SnBRA4WA6jEnGJEtvyNucc","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t## Problem Statement\n2\t\n3\tSomeone running a small website has no self-service way to keep it up to date: publishing an announcement, editing a static page, or controlling who can make content public all require hand-editing HTML or a developer's help. There's also no way to grant a collaborator limited access, or revoke it later, without touching the server directly.\n4\t\n5\t## Solution\n6\t\n7\tA small, WordPress-style web CMS with a local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja2 + SQLite) where Admins and Editors log in and create, edit, delete, and — for Admins — publish Posts and Pages. A `cms publish` / `cms deploy` step renders only the published content to static HTML and pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves as the public site. The admin console itself is never exposed to the public internet. The content model is intentionally generic — this build is not shaped around any specific client; a specific site will be built on top of this CMS afterward, as a separate project.\n8\t\n9\t## User Stories\n10\t\n11\t1. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n12\t2. As an Admin or Editor, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n13\t3. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear error message when I enter the wrong password, so that I know to retry rather than assume the site is broken.\n14\t4. As an Editor, I want my password stored as a secure hash, so that a database leak doesn't expose my actual password.\n15\t5. As an Admin, I want exactly two roles (admin, editor) with different permissions, so that a collaborator can help without being able to break the site or see private account data.\n16\t6. As an Editor, I want to create a new Post, so that I can publish a dated piece of content to the site's feed.\n17\t7. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a draft, so that I can write it over multiple sessions before it's ready.\n18\t8. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post — including one another Editor started — so that a team can collaborate without waiting on the original author.\n19\t9. As an Editor, I want to delete a Post, so that outdated or mistaken content doesn't linger.\n20\t10. As an Editor, I want a live Markdown preview while I write, so that I know what the published post will look like before anyone else sees it.\n21\t11. As an Admin, I want to publish or unpublish any Post, so that I control what the public actually sees.\n22\t12. As an Admin, I want to be the only one who can make content public, so that Editors can draft freely without risking an accidental public mistake.\n23\t13. As an Editor, I want a clear, specific message if I try to publish a Post, so that I understand I need an Admin's help rather than assuming something is broken.\n24\t14. As an Admin or Editor, I want each Post to have a title, a URL slug, a Markdown body, an author, and created/updated timestamps, so that readers and editors know what it is, when it happened, and who wrote it.\n25\t15. As an Editor, I want to create and edit static Pages, so that evergreen site information (e.g. an About page) stays current.\n26\t16. As an Admin, I want published Pages to appear automatically in the public site's navigation, so that I never have to hand-edit a menu when a Page changes.\n27\t17. As an Admin, I want to create a new user account for a collaborator, so that they can start contributing without me editing content on their behalf.\n28\t18. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role between admin and editor, so that responsibilities can shift as a team changes.\n29\t19. As an Admin, I want to deactivate a user's account, so that someone who leaves the team immediately loses access.\n30\t20. As a deactivated user, I want to be refused login with a clear message, so that I understand my access was intentionally revoked, not broken.\n31\t21. As an Editor, I want to be refused access to user-management pages, so that accounts can't be tampered with by mistake or malice.\n32\t22. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing content counts by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n33\t23. As an Admin or Editor, I want to filter the content list by status (draft/published) or type (post/page), so that I can find what I'm looking for without scrolling through everything.\n34\t24. As an Admin or Editor, I want a clear success or error message after every save, so that I know my change actually took effect.\n35\t25. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n36\t26. As a public visitor, I want to see only published content, never drafts, so that I'm not confused by unfinished or incorrect information.\n37\t27. As an Admin, I want a single publish command that regenerates the public site from exactly the currently-published content, so that the live site never drifts from what's actually approved.\n38\t28. As an Admin, I want the published site to use only relative links, so that it works correctly at its GitHub Pages subfolder URL.\n39\t29. As a public visitor or Admin/Editor on a phone, I want the site and admin console to work without horizontal scrolling, so that I can read content or manage it from my phone.\n40\t30. As an Admin, I want any Markdown a user submits to be sanitized before it's rendered anywhere (admin preview or public export), so that a malicious `<script>` tag in a post can't run in anyone's browser.\n41\t31. As an Admin, I want every content-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that a malicious link elsewhere on the web can't silently publish or delete on my behalf while I'm logged in.\n42\t32. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login if I try to reach an admin page directly, so that the admin console is never accidentally exposed.\n43\t33. As the site's operator (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n44\t\n45\t## Implementation Decisions\n46\t\n47\t- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM — none is in the fixed `pyproject.toml` dependency list.\n48\t- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`). Fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author, created/updated timestamps. Slugs unique per kind.\n49\t- **Sessions**: signed, stateless cookies via `itsdangerous` — no server-side session store.\n50\t- **Passwords**: `argon2-cffi` hashing (satisfies rubric D1 directly).\n51\t- **CSRF**: hand-rolled token signed with the same `itsdangerous` utility as sessions, embedded in every state-changing form, verified server-side. No dedicated CSRF library exists in the fixed dependencies.\n52\t- **Markdown/sanitization**: `markdown-it-py` renders Markdown → HTML, then `nh3` sanitizes that HTML. One code path feeds both the admin preview and the static export (rubric D4 checks both).\n53\t- **Access control**: one shared dependency resolves the current user from the session cookie; three guards — authenticated, editor-or-admin, admin-only. Anonymous → redirect to login; wrong role → 403.\n54\t- **Editor/Admin boundary**: Editors get full CRUD (including delete) on any content, including others' drafts, but no publish/unpublish and no user management. Admins get everything Editors get, plus those two.\n55\t- **Publish/export**: `render_site()` extended to emit only published content — Pages at site root (and into the nav), Posts under `posts/` (and into the home feed) — relative paths throughout, respecting `BASE_PATH`. `cms deploy` unchanged.\n56\t- **Demo/seed content**: neutral placeholders only (e.g. a generic site title, example posts/pages) — no client brief, real or fictional, baked into seed data or the schema.\n57\t\n58\t## Testing Decisions\n59\t\n60\t- Assert only on external behavior via `TestClient` (status codes, redirects, response body, cookies) — one documented exception: reading the seeded SQLite file directly to check the `$argon2` hash prefix (D1), per the rubric's own check method.\n61\t- Reuse `client` / `client_as(role)` from `tests/conftest.py`; extend `DEMO_USERS` alongside `scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n62\t- Access-control tests: editor → 403/redirect on every admin-only route; anonymous → redirect to login (D3).\n63\t- CSRF tests: replay one POST per form without the token, assert rejection (D2).\n64\t- Sanitization tests: submit `<script>` + `onerror=`, publish, assert neither survives in the preview or the export (D4).\n65\t- Publish/export tests extend the existing `tests/test_t00.py` pattern (call `render_site()`, assert on filesystem output): published-only, drafts never leak, relative paths only.\n66\t\n67\t## Out of Scope\n68\t\n69\t- Any client-specific content, vocabulary, or data model — this build is a generic CMS engine; a specific site is a separate, later project built on top of it.\n70\t- Revision history with rollback, scheduled publishing — separate `stretch` issues.\n71\t- All other rubric stretch goals not chosen (media uploads, categories/tags, search, comments, plugins, themes, branch+PR workflow, secured live admin deploy).\n72\t- Any public-facing server-side feature (search, comments, live DB) — ADR-001.\n73\t- Hosting the admin console publicly — ADR-001, local-only.\n74\t\n75\t## Further Notes\n76\t\n77\t- This project builds the CMS engine only, with no client in mind, per the instructor's verbal direction (2026-10-01) superseding the earlier client-specific plan recorded in ADR-003 (now marked superseded, kept for the record).\n78\t- Stack fixed by ADR-001/ADR-002, not decided here.\n79\t- Covers all 7 rubric-required capabilities in full; extra credit gets its own issues later.\n80\t</content>\n81\t"}]},"uuid":"c2747888-f9ba-471b-81d2-1b4f8a6c5cfd","timestamp":"2026-10-01T18:13:55.770Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\spec-draft.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nSomeone running a small website has no self-service way to keep it up to date: publishing an announcement, editing a static page, or controlling who can make content public all require hand-editing HTML or a developer's help. As an Admin or Editor, I want the admin navigation to stay visible across admin pages, so that I don't lose my place while managing content.\n26. As the site's operator (Admin), I want to seed realistic demo data (users, posts, pages) with one command, so that I can demo or test the site without manually recreating content every time.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Data layer**: Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, no ORM — none is in the fixed `pyproject.toml` dependency list.\n- **Content model**: Posts and Pages share one schema and one set of routes, distinguished by a `kind` field (`post` | `page`).
