The report follows:\n  SPEC review for T03 complete (12/12 new tests pass; no regressions in full suite — the 8 failing tests are pre-existing unrelated token-budget-exercise stubs).\n  \n  (a) Missing/partial: none. All 8 acceptance criteria have a test that names/exercises it (create-as-draft, cross-author edit, delete, CSRF reject on create/edit/delete via both missing-token-422 and wrong-token-403, script/onerror sanitization, markdown rendering, seed script). The 390px-no-overflow criterion (a visual property, not testable) is consistent with the CSS/markup: textarea width:100%, post-list__item flex-wrap, post-preview__body overflow-wrap:anywhere, no fixed-width elements added.\n  \n  (b) Scope creep: minor only — `.success` CSS class and saved=created/updated/deleted flash messages aren't asked for by the ticket, but are trivial and don't touch any hard constraint.\n  \n  (c) Looks implemented but wrong — real finding: `delete_post` in app/routes/posts.py (~line 354) calls `content_module.delete_content(post_id)`, and `delete_content` (app/content.py line 75) does `DELETE FROM content WHERE id = ?` with NO `kind` filter. Compare to `update_post`/`edit_post_form`, which call `get_content(post_id, KIND)` first and bail if the kind doesn't match, so edit is safely scoped — delete is not. The spec's stated reason for the `kind` field is \"so Pages (T05) needs no migration later\"; as written, once T05 adds `kind='page'` rows, an Editor POSTing to `/admin/posts/{id}/delete` with a page's id would delete that page, since nothing checks it was ever a post. No test catches this today only because no page rows exist yet. `update_content` has the same unscoped-by-kind signature but is incidentally protected by the route's prior `get_content` check; `delete_content` has no such guard. Recommend scoping both by `(id, kind)` to match `get_content`.\n  \n  Everything else (CSRF double-submit, slug uniqueness via `UNIQUE(kind, slug)`, Editor/Admin role boundary, no publish/unpublish UI for Editors) matches the spec faithfully.\n</agent-message>"}

No ORM (see spec Implementation\nDecisions). Posts and Pages share this one table and these functions,\ndistinguished only by `kind` ('post' | 'page') — see CONTEXT.md.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\n\nSLUG_RE = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$\")\n\n\ndef normalize_slug(raw: str) -> str:\n    return raw.strip().lower()\n\n\ndef list_content(kind: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT content.*, users.email AS author_email FROM content \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = content.author_id \"\n            \"WHERE content.kind = ? ORDER BY content.created_at DESC\",\n            (kind,),\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_content(content_id: int, kind: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM content WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\", (content_id, kind)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef delete_content(content_id: int) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM content WHERE id = ?\", (content_id,))\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n CSRF uses the double-submit pattern with the same signer: a\nrandom token is set as a signed cookie and echoed back in the form; a POST\nis rejected unless the submitted value matches what the cookie's signature\nverifies to.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hmac\nimport secrets\n\nfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\nfrom argon2.exceptions import VerificationError, VerifyMismatchError\nfrom itsdangerous import BadSignature, SignatureExpired, URLSafeTimedSerializer\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSESSION_COOKIE = \"session\"\nCSRF_COOKIE = \"csrf_token_signed\"\nSESSION_MAX_AGE = 60 * 60 * 8  # 8 hours\n\n_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n_session_signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.SECRET_KEY, salt=\"session\")\n_csrf_signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.SECRET_KEY, salt=\"csrf\")\n\n\ndef hash_password(raw: str) -> str:\n    return _hasher.hash(raw)\n\n\ndef verify_password(raw: str, hashed: str) -> bool:\n    try:\n        return _hasher.verify(hashed, raw)\n    except (VerifyMismatchError, VerificationError):\n        return False\n\n\ndef sign_session(user_id: int) -> str:\n    return _session_signer.dumps({\"uid\": user_id})\n\n\ndef read_session(token: str | None) -> int | None:\n    if not token:\n        return None\n    try:\n        data = _session_signer.loads(token, max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE)\n    except (BadSignature, SignatureExpired):\n        return None\n    return data.get(\"uid\")\n\n\ndef new_csrf_pair() -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return (raw_token_for_the_form, signed_token_for_the_cookie).\"\"\"\n    raw = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return raw, _csrf_signer.dumps(raw)\n\n\ndef verify_csrf(form_token: str | None, signed_cookie: str | None) -> bool:\n    if not form_token or not signed_cookie:\n        return False\n    try:\n        raw = _csrf_signer.loads(signed_cookie, max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE)\n    except (BadSignature, SignatureExpired):\n        return False\n    return hmac.compare_digest(raw, form_token)\n\n\ndef read_or_mint_csrf(request) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Reuse the request's existing valid CSRF cookie if it has one, so a\n    second page load doesn't invalidate a token already embedded in a page\n    the user still has open. Returns (raw_token_for_the_form,\n    new_signed_cookie_value_or_None) — the caller only needs to call\n    response.set_cookie(...) when the second element isn't None.\"\"\"\n    existing_signed = request.cookies.get(CSRF_COOKIE)\n    if existing_signed:\n        try:\n            return _csrf_signer.loads(existing_signed, max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE), None\n        except (BadSignature, SignatureExpired):\n            pass\n    raw, signed = new_csrf_pair()\n    return raw, signed\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":68,"oldLines":6,"newStart":68,"newLines":14,"lines":["     return hmac.compare_digest(raw, form_token)"," "," ","+def set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie: str | None):","+    \"\"\"Set the CSRF cookie on `response` if read_or_mint_csrf minted a new","+    one (it returns None when the request's existing cookie was reused).\"\"\"","+    if new_cookie is not None:","+        response.set_cookie(CSRF_COOKIE, new_cookie, httponly=True, samesite=\"lax\")","+    return response","+","+"," def read_or_mint_csrf(request) -> tuple[str, str | None]:","     \"\"\"Reuse the request's existing valid CSRF cookie if it has one, so a","     second page load doesn't invalidate a token already embedded in a page"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5f20e9de-9b82-4e0c-bdd2-b6af5580421a","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.290","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

state-changing form —\n`security.read_or_mint_csrf` works for anonymous requests too, keyed only on\nthe request's cookies, not on who's logged in.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Form, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\nfrom app import security, settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\n\ndef _render_login(request: Request, error: str | None, status_code: int = 200):\n    csrf_token, new_cookie = security.read_or_mint_csrf(request)\n    response = templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/login.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Log in\", \"error\": error, \"csrf_token\": csrf_token},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n    if new_cookie is not None:\n        response.set_cookie(security.CSRF_COOKIE, new_cookie, httponly=True, samesite=\"lax\")\n    return response\n\n\ndef current_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    \"\"\"The logged-in user's row, or None. Reusable as a FastAPI dependency.\"\"\"\n    uid = security.read_session(request.cookies.get(security.SESSION_COOKIE))\n    if uid is None:\n        return None\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? AND active = 1\", (uid,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef _user_by_email(email: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\", (email,)).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/login\")\ndef login_form(request: Request):\n    if current_user(request) is not None:\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n    return _render_login(request, error=None)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/login\")\ndef login_submit(\n    request: Request,\n    email: str = Form(...),\n    password: str = Form(...),\n    csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n):\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n        return _render_login(request, error=\"Your session expired — please try again.\", status_code=403)\n\n    row = _user_by_email(email)\n    if row is None or not row[\"active\"] or not security.verify_password(password, row[\"password_hash\"]):\n        return _render_login(request, error=\"Incorrect email or password.\", status_code=401)\n\n    response = RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n    response.set_cookie(\n        security.SESSION_COOKIE, security.sign_session(row[\"id\"]),\n        httponly=True, samesite=\"lax\", max_age=security.SESSION_MAX_AGE,\n    )\n    return response\n\n\n@router.post(\"/logout\")\ndef logout(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(...)):\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n        return _render_login(request, error=\"Your session expired — please log in again.\", status_code=403)\n    response = RedirectResponse(\"/login\", Two-axis review (Standards, Spec) run as parallel sub-agents against the diff: `app/db.py` (new `content` table), `app/content.py` (new), `app/mdrender.py` (new), `app/routes/posts.py` (new), `app/main.py`, `app/publish.py`, `app/seed.py` + `scripts/seed_demo.py`, `templates/admin/base.html`, two new templates, `tests/test_posts.py`.\n\n## Spec axis — one real bug found and fixed\n\n`delete_content` deleted by `id` alone, with no `kind` filter — `update_content` had the same gap but was incidentally protected by the route checking `get_content(id, KIND)` first; `delete_content` had no such guard. Since the ticket's whole reason for the `kind` field is \"so Pages (T05) needs no migration later,\" once Pages exist a Post-delete request could delete a Page that happens to share that row id. **Fixed**: both `delete_content` and `update_content` now take and filter by `kind` in the SQL itself, not just at the call site, plus a regression test (`test_delete_post_does_not_delete_a_page_sharing_the_same_id`) that inserts a `page` row and asserts a `kind='post'` delete call leaves it alone.\n\nEverything else on this axis matched the spec: all 8 acceptance criteria have a test exercising them (create-as-draft, cross-author edit — using a second seeded editor so it's a genuine cross-author check, delete, CSRF-reject on create/edit/delete, script/onerror sanitization, seed script, and the no-overflow-at-390px criterion is a visual property with no test possible, but the CSS/markup — `textarea` at `width:100%`, flex-wrap list items, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the preview pane — is consistent with it). Minor, harmless scope addition noted and kept: flash messages (`saved=created/updated/deleted`) and a `.success` CSS class weren't asked for, but they satisfy spec story 25 (\"a clear success or error message after every save\") and touch nothing risky.\n\n## Standards axis — no hard violations; duplication smells fixed\n\nNo violations of `CLAUDE.md`. The one judgement call worth stating explicitly: `/admin/posts/preview` intentionally skips the CSRF check — the hard constraint is \"every *state-changing* form carries a CSRF token,\" and preview has no side effect (it only echoes back sanitized HTML) and stays behind the `require_editor_or_admin` auth dependency. Confirmed this reasoning holds rather than treating it as a gap.\n\nSeveral Duplicated-Code smells were flagged and fixed:\n- **Fixed**: extracted `_render_post_list()`, now shared by `list_posts` and the delete route's CSRF-failure branch (previously that branch re-implemented the list rendering inline).\n- **Fixed**: extracted `_save_post()`, now shared by `create_post`/`update_post` for slug validation + the duplicate-slug `IntegrityError` handling (previously near-identical in both).\n- **Fixed**: `content.validate_slug()` now folds normalization + the regex check into one function instead of duplicating both steps at each call site.\n- **Fixed**: added `security.set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie)` and switched `auth.py`'s `_render_login`, `main.py`'s `admin_home`, and all of `posts.py` to it, replacing three copies of the same cookie-setting one-liner (the reviewer flagged this as a mild Shotgun-Surgery risk if the cookie flags ever change).\n\nNot changed, as a deliberate scope call: bundling `(post, title, slug, body_md, error)` into a small form-state type (flagged as a Data Clump). Real, but a bigger structural change than this ticket's remaining time justifies; `_save_post`/`_render_form` already collapsed the worst of the repetition. Flagging for a later pass if Pages (T05) needs the same bundle.\n\nFull suite: 45/53 passing. The 8 failures are pre-existing and unrelated: 7 are Exercise B (`usage_report.spend()`, never assigned), 1 is a Windows console-encoding flake in Exercise A's `ctx_guard` hook tests.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1056,"cache_read_input_tokens":180829,"output_tokens":1662,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1056,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1662,"cache_read_input_tokens":180829,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1056,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1056},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_0191VPLJGeT1JzwJSQ7rT9oi":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T03-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\ninput, button, select, textarea { max-width: 100%; font: inherit; }\nform.login-form, form.admin-nav__logout { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 100%; }\nform.admin-nav__logout { display: inline; }\n.admin-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: center; }\n.error { color: #b00020; }\n.success { color: #146c2e; }\ntextarea { width: 100%; }\n.post-form label { display: block; }\n.post-list__delete { display: inline; }\n.post-preview__body { border: 1px solid currentColor; padding: 0.5rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":33,"oldLines":7,"newStart":33,"newLines":7,"lines":[" .post-list { list-style: none; No violations found.\n  \n  **guards.py usage — compliant**\n  `publish_post`/`unpublish_post` use `Depends(require_admin)` exactly the way `require_editor_or_admin` is used elsewhere in this same file (same dependency-injection shape). This is the first real consumer of `require_admin`, and it matches guards.py's documented contract (403 with a specific reason, no redirect); the inline comment explaining that behavior is accurate.\n  \n  **`_apply_status_change` vs. existing helper shape — judgement call**\n  Every sibling helper with more than two params (`_render_form`, `_render_post_list`, `_save_post`) forces keyword-only arguments after `request, user` via a bare `*`. `_apply_status_change(request, user, post_id, new_status, saved_as, csrf_token)` is fully positional, breaking that convention — it's easy to transpose `new_status`/`saved_as` at a call site with no type error to catch it. This is an unnecessary divergence from the file's established shape (task item 3 asked me to judge exactly this), not a hard violation.\n  \n  **Primitive Obsession (baseline smell, judgement call)**\n  `\"published\"` / `\"draft\"` appear as bare string literals in `posts.py` (twice, in `publish_post`/`unpublish_post`'s calls to `_apply_status_change`) and already in `post_list.html`'s `post[\"status\"] == \"draft\"` check, with no shared constant — unlike `KIND = \"post\"`, which this same file *does* centralize. A typo in one of these strings would silently fail to publish/unpublish. Since the file already demonstrates the fix pattern (KIND), this is a reasonable smell to flag.\n  \n  **Shotgun Surgery / duplicated role logic (baseline smell, judgement call)**\n  `post_list.html` adds `{% if current_user[\"role\"] == \"admin\" %}` — the first place in the templates that re-implements a role check that `guards.py`'s `_require_role` already centralizes. It's UI-only (server-side enforcement is still via `require_admin`), but if a role is renamed or a third role is introduced, this check now has to be updated in two places instead of one.\n  \n  **No violations found**: no Duplicated Code between `publish_post`/`unpublish_post` (both are thin and delegate fully to `_apply_status_change`); `set_status` in `app/content.py` matches `update_content`/`delete_content`'s exact connect/execute/commit/finally shape, so it fits the module's existing pattern cleanly.\n</agent-message>"}

The `app/publish.py` CSS line and the `_apply_status_change` helper in `app/routes/posts.py` are proportionate to the feature.\n  \n  **(c) Implemented but wrong/weak:**\n  \n  1. **AC4 — \"A Post's status change persists across a server restart\"** is only nominally tested. `test_publish_status_persists_across_a_server_restart` (tests/test_publish.py:97-112) creates `fresh_app_client = TestClient(create_app())` but never uses it to re-check the post — it's only probed with an unrelated `GET /login`. This technically names a role, so it clears \"not a bare error code,\" but it's the same mechanical string any admin-gated route gets, not a message \"explaining they need an Admin\" for *this* action. The new tests assert only `\"admin\" in response.json()[\"detail\"].lower()`, which the generic string trivially satisfies regardless of how unhelpful it is. The code comment at app/routes/posts.py:176-177 asserts compliance without adding any new copy — it reads as asserting the AC is met rather than actually tailoring the message.\n</agent-message>"}

A wrong role raises a plain HTTPException(403) instead — there's\nnowhere useful to redirect a logged-in user who simply lacks permission.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app.routes.auth import current_user\n\n\nclass NeedsLogin(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by require_login() when there's no authenticated user.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _require_role(user: sqlite3.Row, allowed_roles: set[str]) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    if user[\"role\"] not in allowed_roles:\n        raise HTTPException(403, detail=f\"Requires role: {' or '.join(sorted(allowed_roles))}.\")\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_login(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    user = current_user(request)\n    if user is None:\n        raise NeedsLogin()\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_editor_or_admin(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    return _require_role(require_login(request), {\"editor\", \"admin\"})\n\n\ndef require_admin(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    return _require_role(require_login(request), {\"admin\"})\n","numLines":40,"startLine":1,"totalLines":40}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"25b8c40a-cb82-4192-81e6-d61b8ecf9b60","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.290","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

response = admin.post(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}/unpublish\",\n                           data={\"csrf_token\": csrf2}, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/posts?saved=unpublished\"\n    assert content_module.get_content(post_id, \"post\")[\"status\"] == \"draft\"\n\n\ndef test_editor_cannot_publish_and_gets_a_specific_reason(client_as):\n    post_id = _create_draft(client_as, slug=\"editor-cannot-publish\")\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    csrf =                         follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    post_id = content_module.list_content(\"post\")[0][\"id\"]\n\n    edit_page = response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/posts?saved=unpublished\"\n    assert content_module.get_content(post_id, \"post\")[\"status\"] == \"draft\"\n\n\ndef {"parentUuid":"e4edde30-93c4-463a-b5fa-a03e52864fa1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfkYNsDCu48JGay44fDDB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CTDr1aa4dd35jFwuQnMrd9","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T04-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Two-axis review (Standards, Spec) run as parallel sub-agents against the diff: `app/content.py` (adds `set_status`), `app/routes/posts.py` (adds publish/unpublish), `templates/admin/post_list.html`, `app/publish.py`, `tests/test_publish.py`.\n\n## Spec axis — two real findings, both fixed\n\n1. **The \"persists across a server restart\" test was weaker than the criterion.** It created a fresh `TestClient(create_app())` to stand in for a restart, but then checked the status via a raw `sqlite3` SELECT instead of through that fresh instance's own routes — which only proves `conn.commit()` persists to disk, true for every write since T03, not specific to this ticket. **Fixed**: the test now logs into the fresh client as admin and reads `/admin/posts` through it, asserting the rendered page shows \"Unpublish\" (which the template only renders when it reads `status == \"published\"` back from the db) — so the restarted app's own route/template layer is what's actually being proven, not a side channel.\n\n2. **The 403 message was generic, not action-specific.** The ticket asks for \"a message naming the actual reason (needs an Admin)\" when an Editor tries to publish/unpublish — but the route just reused `require_admin`'s boilerplate `\"Requires role: admin.\"`, which is the same string any admin-gated route would give, not tailored to this action, and the test (`\"admin\" in detail.lower()`) would have passed either way. **Fixed**: `_require_role`/`require_admin` (app/guards.py) now take an optional `detail` override, defaulting to the old generic message so T02's existing tests of them are untouched; `posts.py` defines `_require_admin_to_publish`, which supplies \"Only an Admin can publish or unpublish a Post — ask an Admin to do this for you.\" for these two routes specifically.\n\nNo scope creep found; AC1 and AC3 (admin can publish/unpublish; admin retains full Editor CRUD) were already genuinely exercised.\n\n## Standards axis — no hard violations; three judgement calls fixed\n\nNo CSRF or other `CLAUDE.md` violations; `require_admin` usage matches how `require_editor_or_admin` is already used in this same file.\n\n- **Fixed**: `_apply_status_change` took `new_status`/`saved_as` as plain positional args, the only helper in this file not following the rest's `*`-enforced-keyword-only convention for params past `request, user` — a transposition here (e.g. swapping `new_status`/`saved_as`) would silently do the wrong thing with no type error. Now keyword-only, matching `_render_form`/`_render_post_list`/`_save_post`.\n- **Fixed**: `\"published\"`/`\"draft\"` were bare string literals in two call sites, unlike `KIND`, which this same file already centralizes as a constant. Added `content.STATUS_DRAFT`/`content.STATUS_PUBLISHED` and switched both call sites to them.\n- **Fixed**: `post_list.html` re-implemented the admin-role check (`current_user[\"role\"] == \"admin\"`) in the template, a second place that would need updating if a role were ever renamed. Moved it server-side: `_render_post_list` now computes `is_admin` and passes it in, template just checks the flag.\n\nFull suite: 51/59 passing. The 8 failures are pre-existing and unrelated: 7 are Exercise B (`usage_report.spend()`, never assigned), 1 is a Windows console-encoding flake in Exercise A's `ctx_guard` hook tests.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1038,"cache_read_input_tokens":219968,"output_tokens":1420,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1038,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1420,"cache_read_input_tokens":219968,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1038,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1038},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01CTDr1aa4dd35jFwuQnMrd9":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T04-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Posts and Pages share this one table and these functions,\ndistinguished only by `kind` ('post' | 'page') — see CONTEXT.md.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\n\nSLUG_RE = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$\")\n\nSTATUS_DRAFT = \"draft\"\nSTATUS_PUBLISHED = \"published\"\n\n\ndef normalize_slug(raw: str) -> str:\n    return raw.strip().lower()\n\n\ndef validate_slug(raw: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Normalize `raw` and return it if it's a valid slug, else None.\"\"\"\n    normalized = normalize_slug(raw)\n    return normalized if SLUG_RE.match(normalized) else None\n\n\ndef list_content(kind: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT content.*, users.email AS author_email FROM content \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = content.author_id \"\n            \"WHERE content.kind = ? ORDER BY content.created_at DESC\",\n            (kind,),\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_content(content_id: int, kind: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM content WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\", (content_id, kind)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_status(content_id: int, kind: str, status: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') \"\n            \"WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (status, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef delete_content(content_id: int, kind: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM content WHERE id = ? content_module.update_content(item[\"id\"], kind, title, normalized_slug, body_md)\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n            return _render_form(\n                request, user, item=item, _render_form(request, user, post=None, title=\"\", slug=\"\", body_md=\"\", error=None)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/new\")\ndef create_post(\n    request: Request,\n    title: str = Form(...),\n    slug: str = Form(...),\n    body_md: str = Form(\"\"),\n    csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n    user=Depends(require_editor_or_admin),\n):\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, _render_form(\n        request, user, post=post, title=post[\"title\"], slug=post[\"slug\"],\n        body_md=post[\"body_md\"], error=None,\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/edit\")\ndef user=Depends(require_editor_or_admin),\n):\n    post = content_module.get_content(post_id, KIND)\n    if post is None:\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/posts\", status_code=303)\n    if not _save_post(request, user, post=post, title=title, slug=slug, body_md=body_md,\n                       redirect_saved_as=\"updated\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/delete\")\ndef delete_post(\n content_module.delete_content(post_id, KIND)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/posts?saved=deleted\", status_code=303)\n\n\nPUBLISH_DETAIL = \"Only an Admin can publish or unpublish a Post — ask status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/publish\")\ndef publish_post(\n    request: Request, post_id: int, csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n    user=Depends(_require_admin_to_publish),\n):\n    return _apply_status_change(\n        request, user, post_id, new_status=content_module.STATUS_PUBLISHED,\n        saved_as=\"published\", csrf_token=csrf_token,\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/unpublish\")\ndef unpublish_post(\n    request: Request, post_id: int, csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n    user=Depends(_require_admin_to_publish),\n):\n    return AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_status(content_id: int, kind: str, status: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') \"\n            \"WHERE id = ? Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, Response\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import security, settings\nfrom app.guards import NeedsLogin, require_editor_or_admin\nfrom app.publish import CSS\nfrom app.routes import auth, posts\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(NeedsLogin)\n    def _redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: NeedsLogin):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request, user=Depends(require_editor_or_admin)):\n        csrf_token, new_cookie = security.read_or_mint_csrf(request)\n        context = {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"current_user\": user, \"csrf_token\": csrf_token}\n        response = templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/hello.html\", context)\n        return security.set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/style.css\")\n    def style_css():\n        return Response(CSS, media_type=\"text/css\")\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","numLines":55,"startLine":1,"totalLines":55}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"28625b08-5996-4000-a714-9d5fc3ebcd3e","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.290","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

\"admin/content_form.html\"\n\n\ndef build_content_router(*, kind: str, url_prefix: str, label: str, label_plural: str) -> APIRouter:\n    router = APIRouter(prefix=url_prefix)\n    publish_detail = (\n        f\"Only an Admin can publish or unpublish a {label} — ask an Admin to do this for you.\"\n    )\n\n    def _require_admin_to_publish(request: Request):\n        return require_admin(request, detail=publish_detail)\n\n    def _render_form(request, user, *, item, title, slug, body_md, error, status_code=200):\n        csrf_token, new_cookie = security.read_or_mint_csrf(request)\n        response = templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, FORM_TEMPLATE,\n            {\n                \"title\": f\"Edit {label}\" if item else f\"New {label}\",\n                \"current_user\": user,\n                \"csrf_token\": csrf_token,\n                \"post\": item,\n                \"url_prefix\": url_prefix,\n                \"form_title\": title,\n                \"form_slug\": slug,\n                \"form_body_md\": body_md,\n                \"preview_html\": render_markdown(body_md),\n                \"error\": error,\n            },\n            status_code=status_code,\n        )\n        return security.set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie)\n\n    def _csrf_error(request, user, *, item, title, slug, body_md):\n        return _render_form(\n            request, user, item=item, title=title, slug=slug, body_md=body_md,\n            error=\"Your session expired — please try again.\", status_code=403,\n        )\n\n    def _render_list(request, user, *, saved=None, error=None, status_code=200):\n        items = content_module.list_content(kind)\n        csrf_token, new_cookie = security.read_or_mint_csrf(request)\n        response = templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, LIST_TEMPLATE,\n            {\"title\": label_plural, \"label\": label, \"label_plural\": label_plural,\n             \"url_prefix\": url_prefix, \"current_user\": user, \"posts\": items,\n             \"csrf_token\": csrf_token, \"saved\": saved, \"error\": error,\n             \"is_admin\": user[\"role\"] == \"admin\"},\n            status_code=status_code,\n        )\n        return security.set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie)\n\n    def _save(request, user, *, item, title, slug, body_md, redirect_saved_as):\n        \"\"\"Shared by create and update: validate the slug, write the row,\n        and turn an IntegrityError (duplicate slug) into a form error\n        instead of a 500. `item` is None for create, the existing row for\n        update.\"\"\"\n        normalized_slug = content_module.validate_slug(slug)\n        if normalized_slug is None:\n            return _render_form(\n                request, user, item=item, title=title, slug=slug, body_md=body_md,\n                error=\"Slug must be lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.\",\n            )\n        try:\n            if item is None:\n                content_module.create_content(kind, title, normalized_slug, body_md, user[\"id\"])\n            else:\n {"parentUuid":"d19dd86d-77bd-4cf9-ae14-b4abea5b1a62","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfkZC56sfntgHzNu3gYnR","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014Uz9uA34sRMR475ahxP7a6","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T05-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Two-axis review (Standards, Spec) run as parallel sub-agents against the diff — the main shape of this ticket turned out to be a refactor: extracting T03/T04's Post-specific CRUD/publish/preview logic into a generic `app/routes/content_crud.py` factory (`build_content_router`), with `app/routes/posts.py` reduced to a 10-line call into it and `app/routes/pages.py` added as the symmetric Page caller — plus the nav wiring (`app/publish.py`'s `nav_items()`, `app/main.py`, `templates/base.html`) and `app/seed.py`'s new `seed_pages`.\n\n## Standards axis — no hard violations; one real finding, fixed\n\nVerified the extraction preserved T03/T04's already-reviewed behavior: CSRF checks in the same order, same guard dependencies, same slug/integrity-error handling, relative-paths-only in `nav_items()`. The factory's nested closures were judged idiomatic (FastAPI's `@router.get(...)` registration needs that shared scope), not a smell, and the factory itself isn't speculative generality — CONTEXT.md already states Pages are \"same fields and operations as a Post,\" and this diff ships two real call sites, not a hypothetical one.\n\n**Fixed**: the Python side of the extraction renamed things to generic `item`/`items`, but the template-facing context keys and the two generic templates (`content_list.html`, `content_form.html`) were left using `post`/`posts` as the variable names — so a Page renders through a template whose loop variable is literally called `post`. `CLAUDE.md`'s \"use the vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`... rather than using both\" is unsatisfied by that leftover seam even though the CSS classes and filenames were fully migrated. Renamed the context keys (`content_crud.py`) and both templates to `item`/`items` throughout.\n\nNot changed: `build_content_router`'s four keyword args (`kind`, `url_prefix`, `label`, `label_plural`) always traveling together (a Data Clump) — flagged as minor at only two call sites (Posts, Pages); would be worth a small `ContentKind` type if a third kind ever arrives, not before.\n\n## Spec axis — no missing/partial ACs, no scope creep; one judgement call resolved without a code change\n\nAll four ACs are genuinely exercised: Page CRUD/publish/unpublish with the same role boundaries as Posts, published-vs-draft nav visibility (checked at both the live `/` route and `render_site()`), and `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeding a published \"About\" page. The \"no horizontal overflow at 390px\" AC remains unverified by any test — same pre-existing gap noted on T03/T04's reviews, not made worse by this diff (the generic form template is structurally identical to the old Post-specific one).\n\nOne finding considered and not acted on: `nav_items()` builds page hrefs as flat `{slug}.html`, and slugs are only unique per-`kind` (`UNIQUE(kind, slug)`), so a Post and a Page could share a slug. This isn't a collision in practice: T07's own spec (already drafted, blocked by this ticket) says \"Pages at the site root... Posts under `posts/`\" — different directories by design, so a Post and Page sharing a slug never resolve to the same path once T07 writes files. Leaving `nav_items()` as flat-at-root, since that's exactly where T07 says Pages belong; no defensive namespacing added here that would preempt or guess at T07's own file-layout decision.\n\nFull suite: 62/70 passing. The 8 failures are pre-existing and unrelated: 7 are Exercise B (`usage_report.spend()`, never assigned), 1 is a Windows console-encoding flake in Exercise A's `ctx_guard` hook tests.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1045,"cache_read_input_tokens":286627,"output_tokens":1585,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":92},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1045,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1585,"cache_read_input_tokens":286627,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1045,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1045},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_014Uz9uA34sRMR475ahxP7a6":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T05-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Two-axis review (Standards, Spec) run as parallel sub-agents against the diff — the main shape of this ticket turned out to be a refactor: extracting T03/T04's Post-specific CRUD/publish/preview logic into a generic `app/routes/content_crud.py` factory (`build_content_router`), with `app/routes/posts.py` reduced to a 10-line call into it and `app/routes/pages.py` added as the symmetric Page caller — plus the nav wiring (`app/publish.py`'s `nav_items()`, `app/main.py`, `templates/base.html`) and `app/seed.py`'s new `seed_pages`.\n\n## Standards axis — no hard violations; one real finding, fixed\n\nVerified the extraction preserved T03/T04's already-reviewed behavior: CSRF checks in the same order, same guard dependencies, same slug/integrity-error handling, relative-paths-only in `nav_items()`. The factory's nested closures were judged idiomatic (FastAPI's `@router.get(...)` registration needs that shared scope), not a smell, and the factory itself isn't speculative generality — CONTEXT.md already states Pages are \"same fields and operations as a Post,\" and this diff ships two real call sites, not a hypothetical one.\n\n**Fixed**: the Python side of the extraction renamed things to generic `item`/`items`, but the template-facing context keys and the two generic templates (`content_list.html`, `content_form.html`) were left using `post`/`posts` as the variable names — so a Page renders through a template whose loop variable is literally called `post`. `CLAUDE.md`'s \"use the vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`... rather than using both\" is unsatisfied by that leftover seam even though the CSS classes and filenames were fully migrated. Renamed the context keys (`content_crud.py`) and both templates to `item`/`items` throughout.\n\nNot changed: `build_content_router`'s four keyword args (`kind`, `url_prefix`, `label`, `label_plural`) always traveling together (a Data Clump) — flagged as minor at only two call sites (Posts, Pages); would be worth a small `ContentKind` type if a third kind ever arrives, not before.\n\n## Spec axis — no missing/partial ACs, no scope creep; one judgement call resolved without a code change\n\nAll four ACs are genuinely exercised: Page CRUD/publish/unpublish with the same role boundaries as Posts, published-vs-draft nav visibility (checked at both the live `/` route and `render_site()`), and `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeding a published \"About\" page. The \"no horizontal overflow at 390px\" AC remains unverified by any test — same pre-existing gap noted on T03/T04's reviews, not made worse by this diff (the generic form template is structurally identical to the old Post-specific one).\n\nOne finding considered and not acted on: `nav_items()` builds page hrefs as flat `{slug}.html`, and slugs are only unique per-`kind` (`UNIQUE(kind, slug)`), so a Post and a Page could share a slug. This isn't a collision in practice: T07's own spec (already drafted, blocked by this ticket) says \"Pages at the site root... Posts under `posts/`\" — different directories by design, so a Post and Page sharing a slug never resolve to the same path once T07 writes files. Leaving `nav_items()` as flat-at-root, since that's exactly where T07 says Pages belong; no defensive namespacing added here that would preempt or guess at T07's own file-layout decision.\n\nFull suite: 62/70 passing. Reusable as a FastAPI dependency.\"\"\"\n    uid = security.read_session(request.cookies.get(security.SESSION_COOKIE))\n    if uid is None:\n        return None\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? AND active = 1\", (uid,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef _user_by_email(email: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\", (email,)).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/login\")\ndef login_form(request: Request):\n    if current_user(request) is not None:\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n    return _render_login(request, error=None)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/login\")\ndef login_submit(\n    request: Request,\n    email: str = Form(...),\n    password: str = Form(...),\n    csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n):\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n        return _render_login(request, error=\"Your session expired — please try again.\", status_code=403)\n\n    row = _user_by_email(email)\n    if row is None or not row[\"active\"] or not security.verify_password(password, row[\"password_hash\"]):\n        return _render_login(request, error=\"Incorrect email or password.\", status_code=401)\n\n    response = RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n    response.set_cookie(\n        security.SESSION_COOKIE, security.sign_session(row[\"id\"]),\n        httponly=True, samesite=\"lax\", max_age=security.SESSION_MAX_AGE,\n    )\n    return response\n\n\n@router.post(\"/logout\")\ndef logout(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(...)):\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n        return _render_login(request, error=\"Your session expired — please log in again.\", status_code=403)\n    response = RedirectResponse(\"/login\", {"parentUuid":"3c0a5f64-caeb-4728-93ab-0646887b252c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfkZqhSCHEsUCAFEwuK88","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013jtu7ygjWV3ZaF8u9fn1w3","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T06-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Two-axis review (Standards, Spec) run as parallel sub-agents against the diff: `app/users.py` (new), `app/routes/users.py` (new), `app/routes/auth.py` (login now distinguishes wrong-password from deactivated-account), `templates/admin/base.html`, two new templates, `tests/test_users.py`.\n\n## Spec axis — two real findings, both fixed\n\n1. **Self-lockout footgun, unaddressed.** `change_role`/`deactivate_user_route` never checked whether the Admin was targeting their own account — an Admin could demote or deactivate themselves via these routes with no guard, no warning, and no test, which could leave the system with zero active Admins. The spec text doesn't exclude self-targeting, but it's a real operational hazard worth closing. **Fixed**: both routes now reject `user_id == <the acting admin's id>` with a 403 and a specific message (\"You can't change your own role / deactivate your own account — ask another Admin.\"), plus two new tests.\n2. **CSRF enforcement on `/role` and `/deactivate` was correct in the code but untested** — only `/new`'s CSRF rejection had a test. **Fixed**: added `test_change_role_rejects_wrong_csrf` and `test_deactivate_rejects_wrong_csrf`.\n\nNoted, not changed: `templates/admin/base.html` also gained a `<a href=\"/admin/pages\">Pages</a>` nav link, which the reviewer correctly flagged as unrelated to this ticket — it's a one-line fix for a gap T05 left (the Pages admin UI shipped with no nav link to reach it), bundled here because it's trivial and zero-risk, not because it belongs to T06. Disclosing it explicitly here and in the closing commit rather than hiding it in an unrelated diff.\n\nEverything else checked out: create/role-change/deactivate are each implemented and tested against a real DB row; the deactivated-login message is correctly specific (403, \"deactivated\") while a wrong-password guess against the same account still gets only the generic 401 message (tested explicitly, so deactivation status isn't leaked to someone who doesn't already know the password); `test_editor_is_refused_on_every_user_management_route` is exhaustive against all five routes, not a sample.\n\n## Standards axis — no hard violations; three judgement calls fixed\n\nCSRF tokens present on every form; passwords always go through `hash_password` before touching the DB; nothing logs a plain password. `require_admin` without a `detail` override was judged correct here (unlike T04's publish/unpublish) since every route in this module is uniformly admin-only and \"Users\" isn't even shown in an Editor's nav — there's no \"you can do everything else but this\" exception to explain.\n\n- **Fixed**: `app/users.py::create_user` had no identifier validation, unlike the sibling `content.py` module's `validate_slug`/`normalize_slug` pattern — it relied only on the HTML `type=\"email\"` attribute and the DB's `IntegrityError`. Added `users.validate_email` (normalize + format check), used the same way `content_crud._save` uses `validate_slug`, plus a test for a malformed email.\n- **Fixed**: the role-validity check (`role not in ROLES`) was duplicated across `create_user_route`/`change_role` with inconsistent status codes for the identical failure (default 200 vs. explicit 400). Factored into a shared `_validate_role()` helper and aligned both call sites to the same (default) status code, matching `content_crud._save`'s convention for a validation-redisplay.\n- **Fixed**: the literal `\"Your session expired — please try again.\"` was repeated 3x with no shared helper, unlike `content_crud.py`'s `_csrf_error`. Added `_csrf_error_list`/`_csrf_error_new_form` plus a `CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` constant, used by all three routes.\n\nFull suite: 76/84 passing. The 8 failures are pre-existing and unrelated: 7 are Exercise B (`usage_report.spend()`, never assigned), 1 is a Windows console-encoding flake in Exercise A's `ctx_guard` hook tests.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1034,"cache_read_input_tokens":332728,"output_tokens":1625,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1034,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1625,"cache_read_input_tokens":332728,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1034,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1034},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_013jtu7ygjWV3ZaF8u9fn1w3":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T06-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Login now distinguishes a deactivated account (403,\nspecific message) from a wrong password (401, generic message) so a\ndeactivated user understands their access was revoked without leaking\nthat distinction to someone guessing a password they don't have.\n\nReview added two real safety/coverage fixes: an Admin could previously\ndemote or deactivate their own account via these routes with no guard,\nrisking zero active Admins -- both routes now reject self-targeting.\nCSRF enforcement on /role and /deactivate was correct but untested; added\ntests for both. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\ninput, button, select, textarea { max-width: 100%; font: inherit; }\nform.login-form, form.admin-nav__logout { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 100%; }\nform.admin-nav__logout { display: inline; }\n.admin-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: center; }\n.error { color: #b00020; }\n.success { color: #146c2e; }\ntextarea { width: 100%; }\n.content-form label { display: block; margin-block: 0.75rem; }\n.content-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; }\n.content-list__item { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center;\n  padding-block: 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid currentColor; }\n.content-list__delete, .content-list__publish { display: inline; }\n.content-preview__body { border: 1px solid currentColor; padding: 0.5rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n.site-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items() -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. The linked file itself is written by the full export\n    (T07) — a draft Page never appears here.\"\"\"\n    pages = content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{page['slug']}.html\"} for page in pages]\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n","numLines":72,"startLine":1,"totalLines":72}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"970bd0e2-6f17-48e9-a047-36db2173179d","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.290","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\ninput, button, select, textarea { max-width: 100%; font: inherit; }\nform.login-form, form.admin-nav__logout { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 100%; }\nform.admin-nav__logout { display: inline; }\n.admin-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: center; }\n.error { color: #b00020; }\n.success { color: #146c2e; }\ntextarea { width: 100%; }\n.content-form label { display: block; margin-block: 0.75rem; }\n.content-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; }\n.content-list__item { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center;\n  padding-block: 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid currentColor; }\n.content-list__delete, .content-list__publish { display: inline; }\n.content-preview__body { border: 1px solid currentColor; padding: 0.5rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n.site-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items() -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, Given the codebase's established small-functions convention (content_crud.py factors _render_form/_save/_render_list/_apply_status_change; main.py's own docstring says \"keep this file small\"), render_site() has grown into one function doing three jobs (home feed, post export, page export) with repeated boilerplate. This is a judgement call, not a violation — 40 lines isn't egregious — but it's trending toward Divergent Change (one function now changes for three unrelated reasons).\n  \n  2. **Point 4 — the `site_title | default(title)` fallback papers over the root cause rather than fixing it everywhere.** It correctly fixes public post/page pages (both now pass `site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE` explicitly). But every other caller of base.html still relies on the coincidence that `title == site title`:\n     - main.py's `/` route and publish.py's own index.html render both pass only `title=settings.SITE_TITLE` (no site_title) — correct only because home page's title happens to equal the site title.\n     - Every admin/base.html page (content_form.html via \"Edit Post\"/\"New Post\", content_list.html via \"Posts\"/\"Pages\", admin/hello.html via \"Admin\") still feeds its own page title into the same `title` var the header brand reads — the identical bug this ticket fixed for posts/pages, just pre-existing and untouched. Not a regression, but the fix is now inconsistently applied: two different conventions (explicit site_title vs. accidental default) coexist for the same shared template variable, which is exactly the kind of silent fallback that should have been resolved by passing `site_title` uniformly from every base.html caller rather than defaulting.\n  \n  Minor nit: post.html/page.html use bracket access (`post[\"title\"]`) while other public templates use dot access (`item.href`) — stylistic inconsistency, not a smell on the fixed list.\n  \n  No Mysterious Names, Feature Envy, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest, or Speculative Generality observed. `_feed_items` reuses the \"feed\" term already defined in CONTEXT.md's Post glossary entry — correct vocabulary reuse, not a new term.\n</agent-message>"}

All 8 new tests in tests/test_export.py pass (ran `pytest tests/test_export.py -q` → 8 passed), and the full suite shows no regression — the 8 unrelated pre-existing failures are in tests/test_usage_report.py (NotImplementedError: \"MP2 Exercise B: implement me with /tdd\" — an unrelated unfinished exercise) and tests/test_ctx_guard.py, neither touched by this diff.\n  \n  (a) Missing/partial: none. All five acceptance criteria are met:\n  - \"writes one file per published Post and Page; no draft appears anywhere in site/\" — genuinely exercised by test_publish_writes_one_file_per_published_post_and_page and test_no_draft_appears_anywhere_in_site (the latter greps all rendered HTML for the draft titles, not just checking file existence).\n  - \"Every generated href/src is relative\" — test_every_exported_href_and_src_is_relative scans every *.html under out/ for 'href=\"/' and 'src=\"/', extending test_t00.py's test_published_html_uses_relative_paths pattern to the new post/page files.\n  - \"home page's feed lists published Posts; the nav lists published Pages\" — test_home_feed_lists_published_posts_with_relative_links and test_post_detail_page_links_back_up_one_level both assert on real rendered hrefs (posts/live-post.html, ../live-page.html), not just string presence.\n  - AC4 (live Pages URL) is correctly left untested per the review note — render_site()'s output is structurally sound for it (no hardcoded host/base path anywhere; posts/pages/home all use depth-correct relative hrefs via the new nav_items(prefix=) and _feed_items()).\n  - Test extends tests/test_t00.py's render_site()-then-filesystem-assert pattern, confirmed by reading test_t00.py directly.\n  - BASE_PATH note confirmed by grep: `app/settings.py` defines `BASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")` and it is read nowhere else in app/ or templates/, including this diff — consistent with the deliberate \"relative paths make BASE_PATH unnecessary\" design; not a gap.\n  \n  (b) Scope creep: minor only. post.html renders a `<p><small>{{ post[\"created_at\"] }}</small></p>` timestamp that the ticket didn't ask for, but it's a reasonable, inert addition to a page the ticket does require, not a behavior concern. The base.html header fix (site_title vs title) wasn't an explicit acceptance criterion line-item but is required for home/nav correctness once per-item pages exist, and is directly tested (test_post_and_page_header_shows_site_title_not_the_items_own_title) — appropriately in-scope, not creep.\n  \n  (c) Looks-implemented-but-wrong: none found. Markdown rendering reuses the existing app/mdrender.render_markdown (pre-existing nh3 sanitizer used by admin preview too), so sanitization isn't new/ad-hoc — test_exported_markdown_is_rendered_and_sanitized confirms script/onerror stripped on the actual export path. list_published() orders by created_at DESC (app/content.py:45), giving a sensible most-recent-first home feed. render_site() does shutil.rmtree + mkdir on every call, so stale output from unpublished content is removed — test_running_publish_twice_reflects_current_content_not_stale_output genuinely verifies this by publishing, unpublishing, and re-publishing.\n  \n  No corrections needed.\n</agent-message>"}

As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\ninput, button, select, textarea { max-width: 100%; font: inherit; }\nform.login-form, form.admin-nav__logout { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 100%; }\nform.admin-nav__logout { display: inline; }\n.admin-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: center; }\n.error { color: #b00020; }\n.success { color: #146c2e; }\ntextarea { width: 100%; }\n.content-form label { display: block; margin-block: 0.75rem; }\n.content-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; }\n.content-list__item { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center;\n  padding-block: 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid currentColor; }\n.content-list__delete, .content-list__publish { display: inline; }\n.content-preview__body { border: 1px solid currentColor; padding: 0.5rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n.site-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\n    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\n    never appears here.\"\"\"\n    pages = content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"} for page in pages]\n\n\ndef _feed_items(posts: list) -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    return [{\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\"} for post in posts]\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n\n    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\n    pages = content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=_feed_items(posts),\n            css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n        )\n    )\n\n    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\n    posts_dir.mkdir()\n    post_template = env.get_template(\"public/post.html\")\n    for post in posts:\n        (posts_dir / f\"{post['slug']}.html\").write_text(\n            post_template.render(\n                title=post[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE, post=post,\n                body_html=render_markdown(post[\"body_md\"]),\n                css_path=\"../style.css\", {"parentUuid":"8b83d6d8-915d-46f1-bd9a-bd8289860562","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfkaW9Ny2i9fVbXYtcaqZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017N3rS4CXaobp39U4ncrFBj","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\\scratchpad\\T07-review-comment.md","content":"`/code-review` findings and resolutions, posted before closing this ticket. Two-axis review (Standards, Spec) run as parallel sub-agents against the diff: `app/publish.py` (extends `render_site()`), two new templates (`templates/public/post.html`, `templates/public/page.html`), a fix to `templates/base.html`, `tests/test_export.py` (new, 8 tests — now 9).\n\n## Spec axis — clean, no corrections needed\n\nAll five acceptance criteria are met and genuinely tested: published-only export (with a test that greps all rendered HTML for draft titles, not just checking file existence), relative-paths-only (scanned across every generated `.html` file, not just `index.html`), home feed + nav wiring, and the test extends `tests/test_t00.py`'s exact `render_site()`-then-filesystem-assert pattern. `BASE_PATH` is confirmed unused anywhere in the codebase, consistent with the deliberate design that relative paths work correctly at any base path without needing to read it. AC4 (\"`cms publish && cms deploy` makes the live Pages URL reflect current content\") is an end-to-end deploy claim no automated test can verify here — judged only on whether the output is structurally sound for it, which it is (no hardcoded host, depth-correct relative hrefs throughout). No scope creep beyond a harmless, inert post timestamp.\n\n## Standards axis — no hard violations; one real finding, fixed\n\nVerified `render_site()` reuses the exact same `app.mdrender.render_markdown()` the admin preview uses (no second sanitization path), writes only from `list_published(...)`, and never hand-edits `site/`.\n\n**Fixed**: `render_site()` had grown into one function doing three jobs (home feed, Post export, Page export), with the posts-loop and pages-loop bodies structurally identical apart from the template, output path, and item key — trending toward Divergent Change in a codebase that otherwise factors small, single-purpose functions (`content_crud.py`'s `_render_form`/`_save`/etc.). Extracted `_write_detail_pages()`, now called once for Posts and once for Pages.\n\nOne finding considered and intentionally not acted on: the `site_title | default(title)` fallback in `templates/base.html` correctly fixes the new public Post/Page pages (both now pass `site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE` explicitly), but every other caller of `base.html` — the home page, and every admin page via `admin/base.html` — still feeds its own page title into the same `title` variable the header brand reads, relying on it happening to look right rather than being explicit. This is the same underlying pattern, just pre-existing (shipped since T00/T01) and out of this ticket's scope — fixing it everywhere would mean touching `main.py`'s `public_home`, every `admin/*.py` route, and re-reviewing six already-closed tickets' templates for a cosmetic header-branding concern no ticket's acceptance criteria asks for. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\ninput, button, select, textarea { max-width: 100%; font: inherit; }\nform.login-form, form.admin-nav__logout { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 100%; }\nform.admin-nav__logout { display: inline; }\n.admin-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: center; }\n.error { color: #b00020; }\n.success { color: #146c2e; }\ntextarea { width: 100%; }\n.content-form label { display: block; margin-block: 0.75rem; }\n.content-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; }\n.content-list__item { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center;\n  padding-block: 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid currentColor; }\n.content-list__delete, .content-list__publish { display: inline; }\n.content-preview__body { border: 1px solid currentColor; padding: 0.5rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n.site-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\n    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\n    never appears here.\"\"\"\n    pages = content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"} for page in pages]\n\n\ndef _feed_items(posts: list) -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    return [{\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\"} for post in posts]\n\n\ndef _write_detail_pages(\n    env: Environment, out_dir: Path, *, template_name: str, items: list, item_key: str,\n    prefix: str, css_path: str, home_path: str,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write one file per item using its detail template (public/post.html\n    or public/page.html) — the two loops render_site() needs are identical\n    apart from which key the item is passed under and the relative depth.\"\"\"\n    template = env.get_template(template_name)\n    for item in items:\n        (out_dir / f\"{item['slug']}.html\").write_text(\n            template.render(\n                title=item[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n                **{item_key: item}, body_html=render_markdown(item[\"body_md\"]),\n                css_path=css_path, home_path=home_path, nav_items=nav_items(prefix=prefix),\n            )\n        )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n\n    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\n    pages = content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=_feed_items(posts),\n            css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n        )\n    )\n\n    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\n    posts_dir.mkdir()\n    _write_detail_pages(\n        env, posts_dir, template_name=\"public/post.html\", items=posts, item_key=\"post\",\n        prefix=\"../\", css_path=\"../style.css\", home_path=\"../index.html\",\n    )\n    _write_detail_pages(\n        env, out, template_name=\"public/page.html\", items=pages, item_key=\"page\",\n        prefix=\"\", css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\",\n    )\n\n
