{"parentUuid":"ddb32592-7047-4cf8-b9e5-7abe90c4f1bf","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmSnjLuBy2g9QiAjqBvw","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The new browser tests caught a real bug: on a 390px phone, any Post or Page with a code block, a table or a long URL was about 1100px wide. That affected both the published page and the editor screen. I fixed it in the stylesheet, and all 200 tests now pass (181 before). None of this is committed yet.\n\n**What I added:**\n- **Playwright**, as a dev-only dependency, as you approved.\n- **Phone-width tests** (`tests/test_phone_width.py`, 16 tests): the public home page, a published Post and Page, the login page, 11 admin screens and the editor's 403 page. Each loads at 390px and fails if the page is wider than the screen. This covers the 390px criterion in T01, T03, T05 and T08, and it's the same measurement the grader takes for F3.\n  - **The bug:** the published Post and Page and both editor screens overflowed by 1104 to 1113px. Code blocks and tables now scroll inside their own box, and long words wrap. That's a 5-line change to the CSS in `app/publish.py`, which both the public site and the admin console use.\n- **Live-preview tests** (`tests/test_live_preview.py`, 3 tests), run in a real browser:\n  - the preview renders Markdown as you type,\n  - injected `<script>` and `onerror=` never run in it (the grader's D4 check),\n  - an expired session shows the \"session may have expired\" message instead of the login page (T10).\n\n**Checks I ran:**\n- **The tests can fail.** I temporarily broke the code each test guards: removed the CSS fix, removed the editor's redirect check, and served the preview without sanitizing. Each time the matching test failed, then passed again once the code was restored.\n- **Without Chromium**, the 19 browser tests skip instead of failing, so the suite still passes on a machine that hasn't installed it.\n- **A fresh clone from GitHub** passes all 181 tests from before this work, with no `.env` or database.\n- **`check_submission --stage 2`** passes 19 of 22. The three left are the screenshots and the two tags.\n\nFor your README: anyone who wants the browser tests to run, rather than skip, needs `uv run playwright install chromium` once.\n\n**Two decisions for you:**\n1. **The `cms deploy` and no-secrets-in-history tests.** Your answer only covered Playwright, so I haven't written these. They cover the last untested criteria in T07 and T09. Should I add them?\n2. **How to commit this.** I recommend a T12 ticket: create the issue, run `/code-review`, post the findings on the issue, then commit with `Closes #13`. That keeps the trail the grader checks for B3–B5 consistent with T01–T11. The gaps:\n\n- \"renders without horizontal overflow at 390px\" on T01, T03, T05 and T08 (and rubric F3, which the grader measures in a real browser)\n- T10's live-preview \"session expired\" message, which is in-page JavaScript\n- T07's `cms publish && cms deploy` step, where `cms deploy` has no test\n- T09's \"no `.env` contents, API keys, or other secrets in git history\"\n\nThe layout and preview behaviour can only be observed in a browser, so this adds Playwright as a dev-only dependency (approved by the student) and drives the real app on a local port. Browser tests skip cleanly when Chromium isn't installed, so `uv run pytest` still passes on a clean clone.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The public home page, a published Post and Page, the login page, every admin screen, and the editor's 403 page each fit a 390px viewport (document no wider than the viewport), including with long unbroken words, a long URL, a wide code block, and a wide table in the content\n- [ ] Typing into the editor updates the live preview; script and `onerror=` typed into it never execute\n- [ ] When the session expires while the editor is open, the preview shows the \"session may have expired\" message and never the login page\n- [ ] `cms deploy` pushes `site/` to `gh-pages`, refuses with a clear message when `site/` doesn't exist, and reports a failed push as a non-zero exit\n- [ ] A test fails if any `.env`, `*.db`, or key-shaped token appears anywhere in git history (`.env.example` placeholders allowed), and skips when there is no git history\n- [ ] Browser tests skip, not fail, when Chromium isn't installed\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #12 (T11: Relative links throughout the admin console)\nEOF\n\"/c/Program Files/GitHub CLI/gh.exe\" issue create --title \"T12: Tests for the untested acceptance criteria (phone width, live preview, deploy, secrets)\" --label ticket --body-file \"$TEMP/t12.md\"","description":"Create the T12 ticket issue on GitHub"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"803c1c07-c746-45ae-a285-ad23a0251870","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfmStjAuKQP6B5muYwRpp","type":"assistant","uuid":"da064240-d548-4c79-9e55-57626a1f5584","timestamp":"2026-10-06T18:21:15.404Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.291","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

{"parentUuid":"1462ca6c-6673-4d36-b955-11e46ff6c24e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmSvxinjS2RjpHs5cyzQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011Zk5cxBy8spBQQezyVvwf2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\test_deploy.py","content":"\"\"\"`cms deploy` pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch (T07). Exercised for real\nagainst a throwaway git repo whose `origin` is a local bare repository, so\nnothing ever leaves the machine.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nimport subprocess\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import cli, settings\n\npytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which(\"git\") is None, reason=\"needs git\")\n\n\ndef _git(*args: str, cwd) -> str:\n    return subprocess.run([\"git\", *args], cwd=cwd, check=True,\n                          capture_output=True, text=True).stdout\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef project(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"A git checkout with a published site/ and a local bare `origin`, with\n    the working directory moved into it (ghp-import acts on the cwd's repo).\"\"\"\n    for var, value in {\"GIT_AUTHOR_NAME\": \"Test\", \"GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL\": \"test@example.test\",\n                       \"GIT_COMMITTER_NAME\": \"Test\",\n                       \"GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL\": \"test@example.test\"}.items():\n        monkeypatch.setenv(var, value)\n    origin = tmp_path / \"origin.git\"\n    repo = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n    _git(\"init\", \"--bare\", str(origin), cwd=tmp_path)\n    _git(\"init\", str(repo), cwd=tmp_path)\n    site = repo / \"site\"\n    site.mkdir()\n    (site / \"index.html\").write_text(\"<p>Hello from the CMS</p>\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SITE\", site)\n    monkeypatch.chdir(repo)\n    return {\"repo\": repo, \"origin\": origin, \"site\": site}\n\n\ndef test_deploy_pushes_site_to_gh_pages(project, capsys):\n    _git(\"remote\", \"add\", \"origin\", str(project[\"origin\"]), cwd=project[\"repo\"])\n\n    assert cli.main([\"deploy\"]) == 0\n\n    pushed = _git(\"show\", \"gh-pages:index.html\", cwd=project[\"origin\"])\n    assert pushed == \"<p>Hello from the CMS</p>\"\n    assert \"Pushed to gh-pages\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n\n\ndef test_deploy_without_a_published_site_explains_what_to_do(project, capsys):\n Only typed input is exercised in the browser; the export side is covered by the server tests in `test_export.py`. Fix: open `/admin/posts/{id}/edit` and the exported page for a stored XSS Post, then assert `typeof window.__xss === \"undefined\"`.\n  6. `app/publish.py:27` (judgement call, minor): `table { display:block }` can drop table semantics for screen readers. Fix: leave tables alone and scroll them inside a wrapper, or accept the tradeoff since no admin template uses `<table>`.\n  7. `tests/test_phone_width.py:58` (minor): the login page is only measured in its clean state, not with the wrong-password error showing. Fix: skip when `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints `true`, or reword the docstring.\n  \n  4. **tests/test_no_secrets.py:59, nit.** `--name-only` output is split on whitespace. Fix: use `-z` and `split(\"\\0\")`.\n  \n  5. **tests/test_live_preview.py:27, nit (judgement call).** The `<script>` half of the assertion can never fail: browsers do not run scripts inserted through `innerHTML` (templates/admin/content_form.html:40). Only the `onerror` half tests the sanitizer. Fix: drop the script line, or add a comment saying it is there only for the record.\n  \n  6. **app/publish.py:27, nit (judgement call).** `table { display:block }` can remove table semantics for screen readers in Chromium and WebKit. Fix: accept it for this project, or wrap tables in a scrolling `div` at render time.\n  \n  7. **app/publish.py:25, nit (judgement call).** `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on `body` also breaks ordinary words mid-word in narrow table cells. Fix: scope it to `h1, h2, p, a`.\n  \n  8. **tests/conftest.py:92-95, nit.** Picking a port by binding and then closing a socket leaves a small race before uvicorn binds it. Fix: pass the bound socket to `server.run(sockets=[sock])`.\n  \n  9. **tests/test_phone_width.py:25-31, nit.** `_admin_id` now exists in 6 test files, so it is duplicated code. Fix: move it into conftest beside `DEMO_USERS`.\n  \n  No flakiness found. All waits use Playwright conditions with explicit 5s timeouts, and there are no sleeps. Sessions are stateless signed cookies, each `phone` gets a fresh context, and the app reads `settings.DATABASE_PATH` on every request. So sharing one session-scoped server while each test gets its own database is safe. Nothing in `test_deploy.py` touches the network: origin is a local bare repo under tmp_path.\n</agent-message>"}

the saved-Post test below\n    # covers <script> too, because there the preview is rendered server-side.\n    editor_page.fill(\"#body_md\", XSS_BODY)\n    assert_no_script_ran(editor_page, \"#preview\")\n\n\ndef assert_no_script_ran(page, scope: str) -> None:\n    page.wait_for_selector(f\"{scope} strong\", timeout=5000)\n    # onerror fires after the image fails to load, so wait for that attempt.\n    page.wait_for_function(\n        f\"[...document.querySelectorAll('{scope} img')].every(img => img.complete)\",\n        timeout=5000)\n    assert page.evaluate(\"typeof window.__xss\") == \"undefined\", page.url\n\n\ndef test_saved_post_with_script_never_runs_in_editor_or_export(phone, tmp_path):\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        author = conn.execute(\"SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?\",\n                              (DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],)).fetchone()[\"id\"]\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    post_id = content_module.create_content(\"post\", \"Tricky\", \"tricky\", XSS_BODY, author)\n    content_module.set_status(post_id, \"post\", content_module.STATUS_PUBLISHED)\n\n    log_in(phone, \"editor\")\n    phone.goto(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}/edit\")\n    assert_no_script_ran(phone, \"#preview\")\n\n    exported = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\") / \"posts\" / \"tricky.html\"\n    phone.goto(exported.as_uri())\n    assert_no_script_ran(phone, \"main\")'''\nassert s.count(old) == 1; {"parentUuid":"32a44571-4371-4a4d-a2ad-3274cfcbb7d8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmTctSBibWtFLzF3grzZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WX2wznvSLRETqHrWkM9i84","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > \"$TEMP/t12-review.md\" <<'EOF'\n## /code-review findings — T12\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel: a **Standards** axis (CLAUDE.md, `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary, a Fowler smell baseline, test robustness) and a **Spec** axis (each acceptance criterion against the tests that prove it, plus the backfilled tickets' criteria). All findings were fixed in one batch after both reported.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Standards | `test_deploy.py`'s fixture didn't clear `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`. If pytest ever ran from a git hook, ghp-import's `-p` could have pushed to the **real** repo's `origin` (the live Pages site). Latent, not live. | The fixture now deletes those variables before running anything. |\n| 2 | Standards + Spec | `test_no_secrets.py` only checked that *some* repo existed. It would scan an enclosing repo's history (e.g. the project unzipped inside a grader's repo), pass vacuously on a shallow clone, and pass rather than skip on an empty repo. | Skips unless `--show-toplevel` is this project, the clone isn't shallow, and there is at least one commit. The docstring now says so. |\n| 3 | Standards + Spec | `--name-only` output was split on whitespace, so paths with spaces split apart and non-ASCII paths came back quoted, which could hide a `.db` or `.env` name. | Uses `-z` and splits on NUL. |\n| 4 | Spec | T07's criterion is \"`cms publish && cms deploy` reflects current content\", but the deploy test wrote `index.html` by hand. | The test now publishes a real Post, runs `cms publish` then `cms deploy`, and asserts the Post is on `gh-pages` (home feed and `posts/deployed.html`). |\n| 5 | Spec | D4/T03 mean a *saved* Post's preview and the export; only typed input was checked in a browser. | New `test_saved_post_with_script_never_runs_in_editor_or_export`: a stored `<script>` + `onerror=` Post is opened in the editor (server-rendered preview) and as the exported file. Verified it fails with the sanitizer switched off. |\n| 6 | Standards | The `<script>` half of the typed-preview test can never fail, because browsers don't run scripts inserted via `innerHTML`. | Kept, with a comment explaining that only `onerror` is meaningful there; finding 5 covers `<script>` where it can run. |\n| 7 | Spec | The login page was only measured clean, not with its error message showing. | New `test_login_page_with_its_error_message_fits_a_phone`. |\n| 8 | Standards | `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `body` also broke ordinary words mid-word in narrow table cells. | `td, th { overflow-wrap: normal; }`. Tables now scroll inside their own box, so cells don't need it. |\n| 9 | Standards | Binding a socket to pick a port, closing it, then letting uvicorn re-bind left a small race. | The bound socket is passed straight to `server.run(sockets=[...])`. |\n\n### Deliberately not changed\n\n- **`table { display: block }` can drop table semantics for some screen readers** (both axes, both framed as a judgement call). Kept: no admin template uses `<table>`; tables only come from user Markdown on public pages, and the alternative (wrapping each table in a scrolling `div` at render time) adds post-processing after sanitizing for a minor gain. Trade-off accepted.\n- **Add a `PASSWORD=`/`SECRET` assignment pattern to the secrets scan** (Spec, judgement call). Not added: in this repo that pattern matches code that *reads* secrets from the environment (`CMS_SECRET_KEY` in `app/settings.py`, docs, `.env.example` placeholders), so it would need a growing allow-list to stay green. The real risks — a committed `.env`/`*.db`/key file, or a key-shaped token — are what the test checks, on every branch and including deleted files.\n- **`_admin_id`-style helper duplicated across 6 test files** (Standards, nit). {"parentUuid":"d7a69d43-fa23-44cf-a7b5-fd06e21f24a7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmTgaubT9sSniRC6yn9v","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T12 is done: commit `e2ab2c7` is pushed and issue #13 has closed. All 208 tests pass. On a machine without Chromium, 187 pass and the 21 browser tests skip.\n\n**What the ticket added:**\n- **Phone-width tests:** these caught the editor and published Posts/Pages running about 1100px wide on a 390px phone, which I fixed in the stylesheet.\n- **Live-preview tests:** the preview updates as you type, script never runs in it, and an expired session shows the \"session may have expired\" message.\n- **`cms publish` then `cms deploy`:** the test publishes a real Post and pushes it to a throwaway local git remote, then checks the Post is on its `gh-pages` branch. Nothing touches GitHub.\n- **No secrets in history:** it searches every branch, including deleted files, for a committed `.env`, database or key-shaped token.\n\n**What the two reviews changed:**\n- **A latent risk in the deploy test.** If tests ever ran from a git hook, the deploy test could have pushed to your real repo, and so to the live site. The test setup now clears the git settings that would allow that.\n- **The secrets test** now skips instead of misleading you when the repo is shallow, empty, or inside another repo. It also handles file names containing spaces.\n- **Two more tests:**\n  - a *saved* Post containing script, opened in the editor and as the exported file (the rubric's D4 check),\n  - the login page at 390px with its wrong-password error showing.\n\nI checked that every new test fails when the code it guards is broken, for example with the sanitizer switched off.\n\nI declined two judgement calls and left one small cleanup, each with its reason in the review comment on #13.\n\n**For you:**\n- **README:** anyone who wants the browser tests to run rather than skip needs `uv run playwright install chromium` once.\n- **Uncommitted:** your README edits, `notes/token-budget-plan.md`, the usage ledger and the report.\n- **Budget plan:** your edit is still uncommitted, so `git checkout notes/token-budget-plan.md` would restore the original, as I suggested earlier.\n- **Still to do:** the 12 screenshots, the handoff, and both tags. The checker passes 19 of 22, and those three are what's left.\n- **Deadline:** the Stage 2 deadline is 2:40pm today. If the screenshots won't be ready by then, push `mp2-mvp` before 2:40.\n\nI can take the 12 screenshots with the same Playwright setup if you want."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":273,"cache_read_input_tokens":194206,"output_tokens":834,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":273,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":834,"cache_read_input_tokens":194206,"cache_creation_input_tokens":273,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":273},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"02d8a696-9bd1-41ff-9cda-19133380a766","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfmTgaZkVxTh4ha9Uq7Tk","type":"assistant","uuid":"0c8894ba-a157-4f69-a67b-7381dcf7e02c","timestamp":"2026-10-06T18:31:36.600Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.291","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

Run from the project root:\n\n    uv run python <this file> <project root> <scratch dir>\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport socket\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()\nSCRATCH = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()\nSCRATCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\ndb_path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=SCRATCH)) / \"screens.db\"\n\n# Real env vars win over .env, so the throwaway db and known passwords stick.\nos.environ[\"CMS_DATABASE\"] = str(db_path)\nos.environ[\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\"] = \"screens-admin\"\nos.environ[\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\"] = \"screens-editor\"\nos.environ[\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\"] = \"My CMS\"\nsys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))\n\nimport uvicorn  # noqa: E402\nfrom playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright  # noqa: E402\n\nfrom app import settings  # noqa: E402\nfrom app.main import create_app  # noqa: E402\nfrom app.seed import DEMO_EMAILS, seed_pages, seed_posts, seed_users  # noqa: E402\n\nassert settings.DATABASE_PATH == db_path, settings.DATABASE_PATH\nseed_users(db_path, \"screens-admin\", \"screens-editor\")\nseed_posts(db_path)\nseed_pages(db_path)\n\nsock = socket.socket()\nsock.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\nbase = f\"http://127.0.0.1:{sock.getsockname()[1]}\"\nserver = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(), log_level=\"warning\"))\nthreading.Thread(target=server.run, kwargs={\"sockets\": [sock]}, daemon=True).start()\nwhile not server.started:\n    time.sleep(0.05)\n\nPASSWORDS = {\"admin\": \"screens-admin\", \"editor\": \"screens-editor\"}\nOUT = ROOT / \"docs\" / \"screenshots\"\nOUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n\ndef log_in(page, role):\n    page.goto(f\"{base}/login\")\n    page.fill(\"input[name=email]\", DEMO_EMAILS[role])\n    page.fill(\"input[name=password]\", PASSWORDS[role])\n    page.click(\"button[type=submit]\")\n    page.wait_for_url(\"**/admin\")\n\n\ndef first_post_edit_path(page):\n    page.goto(f\"{base}/admin/posts\")\n    return page.locator(\"a[href*='/edit']\").first.get_attribute(\"href\")\n\n\nwith sync_playwright() as p:\n    browser = p.chromium.launch()\n    for width in (1280, 390):\n        viewport = {\"width\": width, \"height\": 800 if width == 1280 else 844}\n\n        def shot(name, page):\n            page.screenshot(path=str(OUT / f\"{name}-{width}.png\"), full_page=True)\n            print(\"saved\", f\"{name}-{width}.png\", page.url.replace(base, \"\"))\n\n        anon = browser.new_context(viewport=viewport).new_page()\n        anon.goto(f\"{base}/login\")\n        shot(\"login\", anon)\n\n        admin = browser.new_context(viewport=viewport).new_page()\n        log_in(admin, \"admin\")\n        shot(\"dashboard\", admin)\n        admin.goto(f\"{base}/admin/content\")\n        shot(\"content-list\", admin)\n        edit_href = first_post_edit_path(admin)\n        admin.goto(f\"{base}/admin/posts/{edit_href.rstrip('/').split('/')[-2]}/edit\")\n        shot(\"editor\", admin)\n        admin.goto(f\"{base}/admin/users\")\n        shot(\"users\", admin)\n\n        editor = browser.new_context(viewport=viewport).new_page()\n        log_in(editor, \"editor\")\n        response = editor.goto(f\"{base}/admin/users\")\n        assert response.status == 403, response.status\n        shot(\"editor-denied\", editor)\n    browser.close()\n\nserver.should_exit = {"parentUuid":"cbbc72c9-659e-4198-b976-767691dfcc18","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"feabc1a7-ceb6-4e8b-b099-4fddfdf46466","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0119zVg5D6FhNkMzvXZsGjYw","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Route-access guards: authenticated, editor-or-admin, admin-only.\n\nFastAPI dependencies can't return a redirect directly, so an anonymous visit\nraises NeedsLogin, which create_app() maps to a redirect via an exception\nhandler. A wrong role raises a plain HTTPException(403) instead — there's\nnowhere useful to redirect a logged-in user who simply lacks permission.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app.routes.auth import current_user\n\n\nclass NeedsLogin(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by require_login() when there's no authenticated user.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _require_role(\n    user: sqlite3.Row, allowed_roles: set[str], detail: str | None = None\n) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    if user[\"role\"] not in allowed_roles:\n        raise HTTPException(\n            403, detail=detail or f\"Requires role: {' or '.join(sorted(allowed_roles))}.\"\n        )\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_login(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    user = current_user(request)\n    if user is None:\n        raise NeedsLogin()\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_editor_or_admin(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    return _require_role(require_login(request), {\"editor\", \"admin\"})\n\n\ndef require_admin(request: Request, detail: str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"`detail` lets a specific route explain the actual reason for the 403\n    (e.g. \"only an Admin can publish\") instead of the generic role message.\"\"\"\n    return _require_role(require_login(request), {\"admin\"}, detail=detail)\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin; the public site is served at the same\npaths the static export writes. Routes live in their own modules under\napp/routes/ and are included here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app.guards import NeedsLogin\nfrom app.routes import auth, dashboard, pages, posts, public, users\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(dashboard.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n    app.include_router(users.router)\n    app.include_router(public.router)  # last: its /{slug}.html matches broadly\n\n    @app.exception_handler(NeedsLogin)\n    def _redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: NeedsLogin):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\ntests/conftest.py:8:        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\ntests/test_access_control_sweep.py:8:  2. Still a 403;\nanonymous visitors are still sent to login.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tests.conftest import DEMO_USERS, extract_csrf, log_in\nfrom tests.test_admin_links import _assert_links_resolve\n\n\ndef _post_id(client_as) -> int:\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page = admin.get(\"/admin/posts/new\")\n    admin.post(\"/admin/posts/new\", data={\"title\": \"T\", \"slug\": \"t\", \"body_md\": \"x\",\n                                         \"csrf_token\": extract_csrf(page.text)})\n    return 1\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/admin/users\", \"/admin/users/new\"])\ndef test_editor_on_a_user_management_page_sees_an_access_denied_page(client_as, path):\n    response = client_as(\"editor\").get(path)\n\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n    assert response.headers[\"content-type\"].startswith(\"text/html\")\n    assert \"Only an Admin can manage users\" in response.text\n    assert DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"] in response.text  # the admin nav is still there\n\n\ndef test_editor_publishing_sees_the_publish_reason_on_the_page(client_as):\n    post_id = _post_id(client_as)\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    csrf = extract_csrf(editor.get(\"/admin/posts\").text)\n\n    response = editor.post(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}/publish\", data={\"csrf_token\": csrf})\n\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n    assert response.headers[\"content-type\"].startswith(\"text/html\")\n    assert \"Only an Admin can publish\" in response.text\n\n\ndef test_access_denied_page_links_back_and_every_link_resolves(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.get(\"/admin/users/new\")\n    assert 'href=\"../../admin\"' in response.text  # back to the dashboard, relatively\n    _assert_links_resolve(editor, \"/admin/users/new\", response.text)\n\n\ndef test_anonymous_visitor_is_still_redirected_to_login(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin/users\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"].endswith(\"/login\")\n\n\ndef test_other_http_errors_are_unchanged(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/posts/no-such-post.html\")\n    assert response.status_code == 404\n    assert response.json() == {\"detail\": \"Not Found\"}\n\n\ndef test_access_denied_page_fits_a_phone(phone):\n    from tests.test_phone_width import assert_fits_phone\n\n    log_in(phone, \"editor\")\n    phone.goto(\"/admin/users\")\n    assert phone.inner_text(\"h1\") == \"Access denied\"\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1001,"cache_read_input_tokens":213421,"output_tokens":1593,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":205},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1001,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1593,"cache_read_input_tokens":213421,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1001,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1001},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01PJ25yKUDC3itu5xFh1cYAK":{"file_path":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\test_access_denied.py","content":"\"\"\"An Editor who reaches an admin-only page or action gets a real \"access\ndenied\" page in the admin layout, not raw JSON (ticket #14). Still a 403;\nanonymous visitors are still sent to login.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tests.conftest import DEMO_USERS, extract_csrf, log_in\nfrom tests.test_admin_links import _assert_links_resolve\n\n\ndef _post_id(client_as) -> int:\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    page = admin.get(\"/admin/posts/new\")\n    admin.post(\"/admin/posts/new\", data={\"title\": \"T\", \"slug\": \"t\", \"body_md\": \"x\",\n                                         \"csrf_token\": extract_csrf(page.text)})\n    return 1\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/admin/users\", \"/admin/users/new\"])\ndef test_editor_on_a_user_management_page_sees_an_access_denied_page(client_as, path):\n    response = client_as(\"editor\").get(path)\n\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n    assert response.headers[\"content-type\"].startswith(\"text/html\")\n    assert \"Only an Admin can manage users\" in response.text\n    assert DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"] in response.text  # the admin nav is still there\n\n\ndef test_editor_publishing_sees_the_publish_reason_on_the_page(client_as):\n    post_id = _post_id(client_as)\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    csrf = extract_csrf(editor.get(\"/admin/posts\").text)\n\n    response = editor.post(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}/publish\", data={\"csrf_token\": csrf})\n\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n    assert response.headers[\"content-type\"].startswith(\"text/html\")\n    assert \"Only an Admin can publish\" in response.text\n\n\ndef test_access_denied_page_links_back_and_every_link_resolves(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.get(\"/admin/users/new\")\n    assert 'href=\"../../admin\"' in response.text  # back to the dashboard, relatively\n    _assert_links_resolve(editor, \"/admin/users/new\", response.text)\n\n\ndef test_anonymous_visitor_is_still_redirected_to_login(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin/users\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"].endswith(\"/login\")\n\n\ndef test_other_http_errors_are_unchanged(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/posts/no-such-post.html\")\n    assert response.status_code == 404\n    assert response.json() == {\"detail\": \"Not Found\"}\n\n\ndef test_access_denied_page_fits_a_phone(phone):\n    from tests.test_phone_width import assert_fits_phone\n\n    log_in(phone, \"editor\")\n    phone.goto(\"/admin/users\")\n    assert phone.inner_text(\"h1\") == \"Access denied\"\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0a12565a-e193-4c58-abe0-caaa4f4bd592","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.291","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

The standards axis found nothing material: links are relative, the message is autoescaped and server-written, the logout form gets a valid CSRF token, the handler catches only `AccessDenied` (404s and the CSRF 403s are untouched), and a deactivated user with a cookie is still sent to login.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | `app/routes/users.py`'s module docstring still said an Editor gets \"a plain 403\". | Rewritten to describe the Access denied page and its reason. |\n| 2 | Spec | HTML output was proven for only some admin-only routes; the T09 sweep checked status codes only. | Both sweep tests (every admin-only GET and POST route) now also assert the \"Access denied\" page is shown. |\n| 3 | Spec | Link resolution was checked only on a depth-2 page; the publish refusal renders deeper (`/admin/posts/<id>/publish`). | The publish-denied test now resolves every link on that page too. |\n| 4 | Standards | The page looked the user up in the database a second time, though the guard had already loaded it. | `AccessDenied` carries the user; the handler uses it. |\n| 5 | Standards | The new test imported a private helper (`_assert_links_resolve`) from another test module, and had a function-level import. | Helper made public (`assert_links_resolve`); imports moved to the top. |\n| 6 | Standards | `test_other_http_errors_are_unchanged` only checks a 404. | Renamed `test_not_found_is_unchanged`. |\n| 7 | Standards | `_require_admin_for_users` lacked the `-> sqlite3.Row` annotation the guards use. | Added. |\n\n### Deliberately not changed\n\n- **Rendering lives in `app/guards.py` while the `NeedsLogin` handler is in `app/main.py`** (Standards, judgement call). Kept: `guards.py` owns what a refusal *means*, so the exception and how it's shown sit together; `main.py` stays a thin wiring file (its docstring says \"Keep this file small\"), and the `NeedsLogin` handler is a one-line redirect, not a page.\n\n### Verification\n\n- Red first: 5 of the 7 new tests failed before the change (the 2 passing were the guards that login redirects and 404s stay unchanged).\n- Three existing assertions that read the 403 as JSON (`test_pages.py`, `test_publish.py`) now check the page text for the specific \"Only an Admin can publish\" reason, which is stricter than the old `\"admin\" in detail` check.\n- Full suite: **215 passed**. {"parentUuid":"79792c38-0679-4660-b63c-b923338f2a21","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\test_deploy.py","snippet":"5\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n6\t\n7\timport shutil\n8\timport subprocess\n9\t\n10\timport pytest\n11\t\n12\tfrom app import cli, settings\n13\tfrom app import content as content_module\n14\tfrom app import db as db_module\n15\tfrom tests.conftest import DEMO_USERS\n16\t\n17\tpytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which(\"git\") is None, reason=\"needs git\")\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tdef _git(*args: str, cwd) -> str:\n21\t    return subprocess.run([\"git\", *args], cwd=cwd, check=True,\n22\t                          capture_output=True, text=True, encoding=\"utf-8\").stdout\n23\t\n24\t\n25\t@pytest.fixture\n26\tdef project(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n27\t    \"\"\"An empty git checkout (site/ not yet published) with a local bare\n28\t    `origin`, and the working directory moved into it -- ghp-import acts on\n29\t    the current directory's repo.\"\"\"\n30\t    for var, value in {\"GIT_AUTHOR_NAME\": \"Test\", \"GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL\": \"test@example.test\",\n31\t                       \"GIT_COMMITTER_NAME\": \"Test\",\n32\t                       \"GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL\": \"test@example.test\"}.items():\n33\t        monkeypatch.setenv(var, value)\n34\t    # These would point git (and so ghp-import's push) at some other repo --\n35\t    # e.g. the real one, when pytest runs from a git hook. Never inherit them.\n36\t    for var in (\"GIT_DIR\", \"GIT_WORK_TREE\", \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\", \"GIT_COMMON_DIR\"):\n37\t        monkeypatch.delenv(var, raising=False)\n38\t    origin = tmp_path / \"origin.git\"\n39\t    repo = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n40\t    _git(\"init\", \"--bare\", str(origin), cwd=tmp_path)\n41\t    _git(\"init\", str(repo), cwd=tmp_path)\n42\t    site = repo / \"site\"\n43\t    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SITE\", site)\n44\t    monkeypatch.chdir(repo)\n45\t    return {\"repo\": repo, \"origin\": origin, \"site\": site}\n46\t\n47\t\n48\tdef _publish_a_post(title: str) -> None:\n49\t    conn = db_module.connect()\n50\t    try:\n51\t        author = conn.execute(\"SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?\",\n52\t                                   (DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],)).fetchone()[\"id\"]\n53\t    finally:\n54\t        conn.close()\n55\t    post_id = content_module.create_content(\"post\", title, \"deployed\", \"Body.\", author)\n56\t    content_module.set_status(post_id, \"post\", content_module.STATUS_PUBLISHED)\n57\t\n58\t\n59\tdef test_publish_then_deploy_puts_current_content_on_gh_pages(project, capsys):\n60\t    _git(\"remote\", \"add\", \"origin\", str(project[\"origin\"]), cwd=project[\"repo\"])\n61\t    _publish_a_post(\"Fresh off the press\")\n62\t\n63\t    assert cli.main([\"publish\"]) == 0\n64\t    assert cli.main([\"deploy\"]) == 0\n65\t\n66\t    home = _git(\"show\", \"gh-pages:index.html\", cwd=project[\"origin\"])\n67\t    assert \"Fresh off the press\" in home\n68\t    assert \"Fresh off the press\" in _git(\"show\", \"gh-pages:posts/deployed.html\",\n69\t                                         cwd=project[\"origin\"])\n70\t    assert \"Pushed to gh-pages\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n71\t\n72\t\n73\tdef test_deploy_without_a_published_site_explains_what_to_do(project, capsys):\n74\t    assert cli.main([\"deploy\"]) == 1\n75\t    assert \"run `uv run cms publish` first\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n76\t\n77\t\n78\tdef test_a_failed_push_is_reported_as_a_failure(project, capsys):\n79\t    assert cli.main([\"publish\"]) == 0\n80\t    # No `origin` remote, so the push can't succeed.\n81\t    assert cli.main([\"deploy\"]) != 0\n82\t    assert \"Pushed to gh-pages\" not in Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.\n- mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.\n- mattpocock-skills:codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.\n- mattpocock-skills:code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\".\n- mattpocock-skills:resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.\n- mattpocock-skills:wizard: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.\n- mattpocock-skills:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\n- mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a live pane, band, status line, toast or hook inside Claude Code (terminal or desktop Code tab), written as a plugin of function hooks that hot-reloads in this session. Load before writing or debugging a hooks module.\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch\n- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or \"your own browser\"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for \"computer use\". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.\n- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.\n- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.\n- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\n- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \"change it\" or \"add a tab\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\n- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.\n- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.\n- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.\n- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Fix: `outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px;` and drop the box-shadow.\n  2. **should-fix (judgement)**, style.css:10/34: the input, select and textarea border `--border` (#e1e5ee on #fff, about 1.25:1; dark about 1.4:1) fails the 3:1 non-text contrast rule (WCAG 1.4.11). Fix: give form controls a darker border token (for example #8a93a6 light, #4a5368 dark).\n  3. **should-fix**, style.css:189-207: Delete, Deactivate and Unpublish get their styling from context selectors (`.content-list__delete button`, `.content-list__publish--off button`). Meanwhile `.button--danger` is dead, because no template uses it. Fix: put `button--danger` and `button--secondary` on those buttons and delete the context selectors.\n  4. **should-fix (scope, judgement)**: this \"visual only\" ticket also changes what the UI does. It adds an \"All content\" nav link (admin/base.html), stat links with `?status=` filters, quick actions and a \"Welcome back\" line (dashboard.html), back links, autocomplete attributes (login.html), and post dates on the public home feed (publish.py:53-54). Every link targets an existing route, but these changes should be named in the ticket comment or commit message.\n  5. **nit**, style.css:144/269/311/354/296: the same surface block (surface, border, radius, shadow) is repeated 5 times. Fix: one shared selector list.\n  6. **nit**, style.css:68: `:focus-visible { border-radius: 6px }` overrides the 9px radius on `<button>`, because the element selector loses on specificity. Fix: remove that declaration.\n  7. **nit**, style.css:333: `top: 5rem` is a magic number tied to the topbar height. Fix: put it in a `--topbar-h` token.\n  8. **nit**, style.css:67: `.muted` is unused. Delete it.\n  9. **nit**: dates are trimmed with `[:10]` in two places, publish.py:54 and post.html:5. Fix: trim in one place.\n  10. **nit**, post.html:8: the decorative \"←\" in \"← All posts\" is not `aria-hidden`. Fix: wrap it in `<span aria-hidden=\"true\">`.\n  11. **nit**, login.html:3: the \"Admin console\" brand links to the public `index.html`. Fix: label it with the site title, or link it to `admin`.\n  12. **nit**, publish.py:22: the extra parentheses are redundant, and CSS is read once at import, so edits need a server restart. Acceptable.\n  \n  Colour contrast (estimated) passes AA everywhere:\n  \n  | Element | Light | Dark |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | Muted text on white | 5.7 | 6.9 |\n  | Muted text on muted surface | 5.05 | 6.3 |\n  | Draft badge | 4.7 (tightest) | – |\n  | Published badge | 4.9 | – |\n  | Admin badge | 5.55 | 5.0 |\n  | Danger on soft background | 5.0 | – |\n  | Button text on accent | 6.3 | 6.4 |\n  \n  `aria-hidden` is on both ✦ marks, and `aria-current` is used correctly in the admin nav (the public nav has none; optional).\n  \n  The tests were adapted, not weakened. `_visible_text` still asserts the exact \"N drafts / N published\" strings. `brand_text` checks equality with SITE_TITLE, which is stricter than the old substring check. The relative-path and draft assertions are unchanged apart from `encoding=\"utf-8\"`.\n</agent-message>"}

The radius override was removed too (finding 6). |\n| 2 | Standards | Form-control borders (`#e1e5ee` on white, about 1.25:1) failed WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for UI components. | New `--control-border` token (`#8a93a6` light, `#5a647a` dark) for inputs, selects and textareas. |\n| 3 | Standards | Delete, Deactivate and Unpublish were styled by context selectors, and `.button--danger` was dead. | The buttons carry `button--danger` / `button--secondary`; the context selectors are gone. |\n| 4 | Standards | The same surface block (background, border, radius, shadow) was repeated 5 times. | One shared rule for `.card, .content-list, .content-filters, .stat, .post-card`. |\n| 5 | Standards | `top: 5rem` was a magic number tied to the top bar's height. | `--topbar-h` token. |\n| 6 | Standards | `:focus-visible { border-radius: 6px }` overrode button radii. | Removed. |\n| 7 | Standards | `.muted` was unused. | Removed. |\n| 8 | Standards | Dates were trimmed with `[:10]` in two places. | One `_date()` helper in `app/publish.py` feeds both the home feed and Post pages. |\n| 9 | Standards | The decorative \"←\" in \"← All posts\" was read aloud. | Wrapped in `aria-hidden=\"true\"`. |\n| 10 | Both | The login page's \"Admin console\" brand linked to the public `index.html`. | Links to `admin` like every other admin page. |\n| 11 | Spec | The seeded Welcome Post showed its title twice (the title, then `# Welcome` in the body). | Seed body no longer repeats the heading. Fresh seeds only; existing databases are untouched. |\n| 12 | Spec | Nothing tested the new current-section marking. | `test_admin_nav_marks_the_current_section` (6 cases): exactly one `aria-current=\"page\"` link, on the right section. |\n| 13 | Standards | Redundant parentheses around `Path(...)` in `publish.py`. | Removed. |\n\n### Disclosed: small usability additions beyond pure styling (both axes)\n\nBoth reviewers noted that a few changes do more than restyle. All are additive, all use **existing routes**, and no permission, form field, or content rule changed:\n- an \"All content\" link in the admin nav (the route existed since T08);\n- dashboard stat tiles link to the matching `?status=` filtered list, plus quick \"New post / New page / View all content\" buttons and a \"Welcome back\" line;\n- \"Back to list\", \"Back to users\" and \"← All posts\" links;\n- `autocomplete` hints on the login fields;\n- the public home feed shows each Post's date.\n\nKept because they serve the ticket's \"friendlier\" goal, and named here and in the commit message.\n\n### Deliberately not changed\n\n- **The `content-list-*` screenshots show the filtered \"All content\" overview, which has no Delete button** (Spec, judgement call). Kept: the rubric's \"content list\" is the filterable list C5 describes, which is that screen. Delete styling is visible in `users-*` (Deactivate) and was checked separately on `/admin/posts` in light and dark.\n- **CSS is read once at import, so stylesheet edits need a server restart** (Standards; the reviewer called it acceptable). Kept for simplicity.\n\n### Verification\n\n- Full suite: **221 passed** (215 before + 6 nav tests). Every page still fits 390px, every link stays relative, and `check_submission.py`'s root-absolute check passes.\n- Test changes are adaptations, not weakenings (confirmed by both axes):\n  - the dashboard tests assert the same \"N drafts / N published\" text, as a reader sees it;\n  - the brand test now requires equality with the site title, which is stricter;\n  - export tests read files as UTF-8 explicitly. They used Windows' default encoding, which breaks on the new non-ASCII glyphs.\n- The editor's new two-column grid initially let a wide code block push past 390px. The existing phone-width tests caught it, and it is fixed with `minmax(0, 1fr)`.\n- All 12 screenshots were retaken against the final code.\nEOF\n\"$GH\" issue comment 15 --body-file \"$TEMP/t14-review.md\" && git add app/publish.py app/style.css app/seed.py templates/base.html templates/admin/access_denied.html templates/admin/base.html templates/admin/content_form.html templates/admin/content_list.html templates/admin/content_overview.html templates/admin/dashboard.html templates/admin/login.html templates/admin/user_form.html templates/admin/user_list.html templates/public/home.html templates/public/page.html templates/public/post.html tests/test_dashboard.py tests/test_export.py tests/test_pages.py tests/test_t00.py tests/test_admin_links.py docs/screenshots/*.png && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT14: Friendlier visual design for the admin console and public site\n\nA visual and usability pass over every screen. One stylesheet, now its\nown file (app/style.css), styles both the admin console and the export,\nwith light and dark colour schemes: a top bar with current-section\nnavigation, stat tiles on the dashboard, tidy content and user rows with\nstatus badges, label-over-field forms with visible focus, styled\nsuccess/error banners, a side-by-side editor and live preview on wide\nscreens, and card-style public pages.\n\nSmall usability additions, all on existing routes: an \"All content\" nav\nlink, stat tiles linking to filtered lists, quick-create buttons, back\nlinks, login autocomplete hints, and dates on the public home feed. Log in with the passwords in your `.env`.\n- http://localhost:8000/ for the public site, exactly as it will export.\n\nTo put it live:\n\n```bash\nuv run cms publish\nuv run cms deploy\n```\n\nA few things to know:\n- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 doesn't support `&&`.** Run the two commands one after the other, or join them with `;`. {"parentUuid":"2d038313-734c-493e-83aa-97ed78a0f703","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnGFLdtNMFWPMDLDpZC7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Confirmed. Your `PYTHONPATH` is set at both the user and the machine level to Python 3.12's `site-packages`. That folder contains `argparse.py`, an old copy of the PyPI `argparse` backport. Because `PYTHONPATH` takes priority over everything else, every Python on your machine, including the project's own `.venv`, loads that outdated file instead of the real standard-library `argparse`. The old copy doesn't understand `required=`, hence the error.\n\nIt's also why we've needed `export PYTHONPATH=` before every `uv run` all along.\n\n**To run it now (this terminal only):**\n```powershell\n$env:PYTHONPATH = \"\"\nuv run cms serve\n```\nIn Git Bash, use `export PYTHONPATH=` instead.\n\n**To fix it permanently,** do either or both of these. They change your global Python setup, so I haven't touched them:\n1. **Remove the backport.** It's useless on Python 3, because `argparse` has been built in since 3.2:\n   ```powershell\n   py -3.12 -m pip uninstall argparse\n   ```\n2. **Delete the `PYTHONPATH` variable** in *Start → \"Edit the system environment variables\" → Environment Variables*, at both the user and the system level. Pointing it at Python's own `site-packages` does nothing useful, because Python already searches there, and it breaks every virtual environment. Removing the system-level one needs admin rights. Open a new terminal afterwards.\n\nThis only affects your machine. The grader's clean Linux setup has no `PYTHONPATH` set, which is why the fresh-clone runs passed."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1238,"cache_read_input_tokens":353308,"output_tokens":764,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":228},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1238,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":764,"cache_read_input_tokens":353308,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1238,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1238},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"3d0abeaa-bee1-4167-bdff-495ba556a73b","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfnGFLJJ8vzreoBJn17BD","type":"assistant","uuid":"d95e2ce1-1510-4858-b28e-9b8f81e9e625","timestamp":"2026-10-07T04:42:14.037Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main","slug":"proud-herding-wadler"}

MP2 is Pass/No-Pass at 70, and the rubric says extra credit \"counts only if the score is ≥70 without it; it can raise a Pass, never create one.\" If you're comfortably passing already, which every check so far suggests, extra credit only moves the number.\n\n**The rules (rubric §5):** up to 5 points. Each stretch goal needs:\n- its own GitHub issue labelled `stretch` (the label already exists in your repo),\n- passing tests,\n- a `/code-review` comment posted before the issue closes.\n\n**The menu, and how each fits this project:**\n\n| Stretch goal | Pts | Fit |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Revision history with rollback** | 2 | ✅ Already planned: your spec (#1) names it as a future `stretch` issue |\n| **Scheduled publishing** | 1 | ✅ Also named in your spec. One caveat for a static site: a scheduled Post goes live the next time `cms publish` runs after its time, not on its own |\n| **Last two tickets as branch + pull request** | 1 | ✅ Nearly free if the two goals above are done on branches and merged by PR, since they'd *be* the last two tickets |\n| Switchable theme | 1 | Possible and cheap (a light/dark toggle), but your spec lists it as not chosen |\n| Media uploads, categories/tags, site search | 1 each | Your spec lists these as not chosen |\n| Plugin/hook system | 2 | Not chosen; its grading is vague |\n| Comments with moderation | 2 | ❌ ADR-001 rules out server-side features on the public site |\n| Live admin deploy | 2 | ❌ Contradicts CLAUDE.md and ADR-001: the admin console never goes on the public internet |\n\n**My recommendation:** do what your spec already planned. Revision history (2) and scheduled publishing (1), each as a `stretch` issue built on its own branch and merged by PR (+1), adds up to **4 points**. It also keeps the trail consistent: the spec said these come later as `stretch` issues, so doing them proves the plan was followed.\n\n**Time and risk:** it's about 1am, and the deadline is 2:40pm. With tests, both reviews and the PRs, that's about 2–3 hours of work. To keep it safe:\n1. **Commit your required items first:** the report, handoff, session 05 transcript and ledger. Then `main` is submittable at any moment.\n2. **Build each goal on a branch,** and merge only when its tests and reviews pass. If time runs short, skip whatever isn't merged.\n3. **Tag `mp2-final` after the last merge,** well before 2:40pm. {"parentUuid":"97657685-3243-40ac-bd1c-61f0916f9be6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnHoETaAPjPZK81AkB9E","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011rvNDFy1xgXwk68NdtrcNg","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\02_extra-credit_20261007.md","content":"# Handoff: IPHS 400 MP2 CMS, extra credit (stretch goals)\n\n**Written:** 2026-10-07, about 1:00am EDT\n**Repo:** `C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms` → https://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms\n**Hard deadline:** `mp2-final` tag pushed and email sent by **2026-10-07 2:40pm EDT** (end of grace). Extra credit only counts if it is merged *before* the tag is created.\n\n## Goal of this session\n\nEarn up to 4 extra-credit points (rubric `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` §5) with the two stretch goals the spec already planned. Spec issue #1, \"Out of Scope\" and \"Further Notes\", says they come later as `stretch` issues.\n\n1. **Revision history with rollback** (2 pts)\n2. **Scheduled publishing** (1 pt)\n3. **\"Last two tickets done as branch + pull request\"** (1 pt): build 1 and 2 on their own branches and merge each through a PR, so they are the last two tickets.\n\nThe rubric rule for each stretch goal: its own issue labelled **`stretch`** (the label exists), passing tests, and a `/code-review` findings comment posted on the issue **before it closes**. MP2 is Pass/No-Pass at 70, so extra credit can't change the outcome. **Never let it put a submittable `main` at risk.**\n\n## State at handoff\n\n- `main` is at `b2539ee` (T14) and pushed. T01–T14 = issues #2–#15, all closed; spec #1 stays open on purpose.\n- **Tests:** 221 pass (`uv run pytest`). The Playwright browser tests run here because Chromium is installed.\n- **Rubric walkthrough:** a fresh-clone run of C1–C7, D1, D2, D4, F1, F2 and F4 passed 42/42 before T14.\n- **Checker:** `check_submission.py --stage 2` passes 21/22; only `mp2-final` is missing.\n- **The student's own uncommitted items:** the report, handoff 01, the session 05 transcript, and the usage ledger. Advice already given:\n  - commit these *before* starting extra credit, so `main` is submittable at any moment;\n  - do **not** commit the raw `docs/transcripts/*.jsonl`, which breaks the H2 naming pattern.\n- The live Pages site may still show the pre-T14 design. The student was told how to run `cms publish` / `cms deploy` themselves.\n\n## How work is done in this repo (follow exactly)\n\n- Read `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` first. `CLAUDE.md` holds the hard rules: relative paths only, CSRF on every state-changing form, sanitized Markdown, only published content reaches `site/`, ask before adding a dependency.\n- **Ticket flow, as done for T10–T14** (see any of issues #11–#15 for the issue body format and the review-comment format):\n  1. Create the issue first, labelled `stretch`. Use the body sections Parent / What to build / Acceptance criteria / Blocked by.\n  2. TDD at agreed seams: red first, and confirm the seams with the student before writing tests (`mattpocock-skills:tdd`).\n  3. Two-axis `/code-review`: two parallel background sub-agents, one Standards and one Spec. Wait for both, then fix in one batch.\n  4. Post the findings and how each was resolved as a comment on the issue, **before** merging.\n  5. Merge through a PR whose body or merge commit says `Closes #N`. The commit/PR title should start with the ticket id. The next ids are T15 and T16, since CLAUDE.md wants the `T0N:` style.\n- **Branch + PR:** `git switch -c t15-revision-history` → commit → `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` → merge (`gh pr merge --merge`) only once tests and the review comment are done. **Never force-push.** Never commit straight to `main` for these two.\n- Stage files explicitly; never `git add -A`. `README.md` is the student's alone. Never commit `.env`, `*.db` or `grading_prompt.md` (it is excluded via `.git/info/exclude`).\n\n## Design notes for the two features (decide details with the student)\n\n- **Schema change needs a migration.** `app/db.py` creates tables with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so new tables are fine. A new *column* on `content` (e.g. `publish_at`) needs an `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` path, or existing `cms.db` files, including the student's, won't have it.
